title: Adaptive Quantum Machine Learning Model Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum machine learning model optimization method designed to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters based on model performance. Traditional machine learning optimization methods rely on manual parameter design, while this approach leverages the unique capabilities of quantum self-adapted machine learning models to achieve significantly improved model accuracy. The core mechanism involves a quantum optimization process that adapts to the model's internal state, allowing for efficient parameter refinement. This research explores the potential of quantum algorithms to enhance the optimization process, addressing key challenges in traditional machine learning. The paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: L’informatique quantique au service de la pharmacie : Promesses, expérimentations et premiers enseignements industriels
abstract: La seconde révolution quantique ouvre des perspectives nouvelles pour l’industrie pharmaceutique, notamment en simulation moléculaire, optimisation et machine learning . Fondé sur des expérimentations menées chez Servier, cet article présente une analyse critique de l’état réel de la technologie, de ses limites actuelles et des trajectoires d’adoption envisageables. Il met en évidence le rôle central des approches hybrides à court terme, les conditions d’un avantage quantique ciblé à moyen terme, ainsi que les enjeux scientifiques, industriels et de souveraineté, associés à ces développements.

title: Quantenbasierte Infrastruktur Netze für Sicherheitskritische drahtlose Datenkommunikation (QuINSiDa); Teilvorhaben: KEEQuant
abstract: Im Teilvorhaben von KEEQuant im Verbundprojekt QuINSiDa wurden ein CV-QKD-basierter Freistrahlpfad, ein Schlüsselmanagement-System (KMS) sowie die zugehörigen Schnittstellen zu Li-Fi, PAT-System, Monitoring und Kryptographieeinheit für einen demonstratororientierten Aufbau zur quantengesicherten drahtlosen Anbindung auf den „letzten Metern“ erarbeitet. Die Arbeiten umfassten Konzept, Schnittstellenentwicklung, bilaterale Tests und Verbundintegration; projektabschließend wurden die Teilkomponenten in einer Gesamtdemonstration in Dresden zusammengeführt. Damit wurden belastbare technische und integrative Grundlagen für weiterführende Anschlussarbeiten geschaffen.

title: Prediction and Visualization of Patient Readmission Risk
abstract: The aim of the thesis is to predict the risk of hospital readmission within 30 days after discharge and to visualize the corresponding results. The medical database MIMIC-IV, version v3.1, was used for the study, from which a final sample of 534,227 hospital admissions was formed. Due to the large volume and complexity of the data, the main preprocessing stage was implemented in an Apache Spark environment using PySpark. An extensive set of features was created, including demographic information, patient flow across care units, history of previous hospital admissions, laboratory values, medication data, and polypharmacy. In addition, composite clinical indicators were calculated, including eGFR, FIB-4, the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and the Comorbidity Burden Score. A key contribution of this thesis is the semantic representation of diagnoses and medical procedures. For this purpose, the textual descriptions of the CCS/CCSR categories were used. These descriptions were transformed into embeddings using ClinicalT5-Large, followed by the application of PCA, UMAP, and KMeans in order to create semantic groups of diagnoses and procedures. These groups generated 45 new features, while the local large language model Qwen3, through Ollama, was used to produce short clinical labels for improved interpretation and visualization in Power BI. For the prediction of readmission risk, the XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost models were trained. Class imbalance was addressed through appropriate weighting, while the final classification threshold was selected based on Youden’s J criterion on the validation set. SHAP values were used to interpret the predictions both globally and at the level of individual hospital admissions, and were subsequently incorporated into a Power BI dashboard. The results showed that LightGBM achieved the best performance in both experimental versions. The baseline version, consisting of 937 features, achieved an AUROC of 0.7766, while the version with 382 features, including 45 features derived from the ClinicalT5 semantic clusters, achieved an AUROC of 0.7702.

title: A privacy preserving federated meta ensemble stacking framework with explainability and differential privacy for chronic kidney disease prediction in resource constrained settings
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health concern that requires early and reliable diagnosis to reduce disease progression and associated complications. Existing machine learning approaches often rely on centralized training, limiting their applicability in healthcare environments where data privacy, heterogeneity, and resource constraints are critical concerns. To address these challenges, this study proposes a privacy-preserving federated meta-ensemble stacking framework for CKD prediction. The proposed approach integrates a hybrid preprocessing pipeline, federated learning with prediction-level aggregation, differential privacy, and SHAP-based explainability to enable secure, interpretable, and decentralized model learning. Experimental evaluation demonstrates a mean cross-validation accuracy of 98.85% with an F1-score of 98.58%. The framework maintains robust performance under Gaussian noise, achieving 97.50% accuracy, while cross-client evaluation reaches 99.25%, demonstrating strong generalization across distributed healthcare institutions. The model also exhibits excellent discrimination and calibration, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.998, PR-AUC of 0.997, and a Brier score of 0.00038. Furthermore, communication overhead is reduced from 0.82 MB to 0.25 MB through compression and sparse updates. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an accurate, privacy-aware, and interpretable solution for decentralized CKD prediction.

title: Corten - Foundational Verification of Rust Programs
abstract: We present Corten, a foundational verification framework for Rust programs in the Rocq theorem prover, built on the Iris separation logic framework. Corten provides the first semantics of surface-level Rust mechanized in a proof assistant with an attached program logic, directly grounded in the Rust Reference: it deeply embeds the Typed High-level Intermediate Representation (THIR) into Rocq and formalises Rust's dynamic semantics as a weakest-precondition predicate transformer calculus. By operating at THIR rather than on internal compiler representations, Corten proof goals display the THIR AST, which pretty-prints to surface Rust, keeping verification close to the source code and facilitating maintainability as code evolves. Atop this semantics, Corten develops a program logic and a syntax-directed proof automation layer; the program logic includes defunctionalized continuation stacks that keep proof goals first-order and compact. Soundness is established incrementally, construct by construct, against an interaction-trees denotation. A synthetic test suite demonstrates a two-to-four times reduction in proof size compared to raw semantic proofs. We further showcase Corten on a buddy allocator case study, verifying memory safety of the allocation and deallocation functions, laying the groundwork for end-to-end verification in a shared Rocq semantic foundation spanning hardware-software boundaries.

title: Stable and Scalable Bundle Adjustment of Holistic 3D Structures
abstract: Bundle Adjustment (BA) is a cornerstone of 3D computer vision and has benefited from decades of advances in sparse optimization and numerical methods. It was originally developed for jointly optimizing camera intrinsics, poses and sparse 3D points. While extensions incorporate lines and other primitives, integrating richer geometric structures such as parallelism, coplanarity, or wireframes often introduces significantly increased computational cost and reduced numerical stability. In this paper, we propose a unified framework that extends bundle adjustment to jointly optimize geometric features and higher-order relations. We first introduce a taxonomy that distinguishes scalable geometric features with direct 2D measurements (e.g., points and lines), from groups encoding higher-order relations (e.g., coplanarity, parallelism, etc.), where we show that groups can be modeled as camera-like entities within the bundle adjustment framework. Building on this formulation, we propose that both group constraints and cross-feature relations (i.e., point-line associations) can be expressed through 2D reprojection measurements. By formulating group-induced and cross-feature reprojection errors, we preserve the sparsity structure of classical point-based BA under Schur elimination, while avoiding direct 3D regularization that degrades the conditioning and stability. Experiments on both real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate runtime performance comparable to classical point-only bundle adjustment, while producing significantly richer 3D structures and improved geometric accuracy.

title: Practice Makes (Im)Perfect: A Look Back at Benchmarking Practices for Microarchitectural Side-Channel Attacks
abstract: Microarchitectural side-channel research has grown at an exceptional pace in recent years, increasing the need for rigorous and meaningful benchmarking. Early attack papers typically relied on indirect proxies, such as covert-channel bandwidth or key-recovery on naive AES and RSA implementations, setting de facto standards that many subsequent works continued to replicate, sometimes by directly comparing against raw numbers from prior work. While these practices offer convenient points of comparison, current benchmarks may not be the most relevant to assess specific properties of new primitives. Even more problematic, microarchitectural attacks are notoriously sensitive to experimental conditions: minimal changes in the target system can significantly alter outcomes and performance. As a result, inadequate evaluation practices undermine reproducibility and cast doubt on the relevance of comparisons, even in top-tier venues where such issues should be identified. This paper tackles the core problem of proper benchmarking for microarchitectural side-channel attacks and examines its broader impact on research quality in the field. We survey 83 attack papers published in top-ranked security and architecture conferences from 2014 to 2024. From this corpus, we identify and define 19 recurrent benchmarking flaws that affect evaluation completeness, relevance, soundness, and reproducibility. These flaws include unfair or absent comparisons, missing code or materials, and the failure to evaluate the key attack properties. On average, each paper exhibits 5.5 such flaws, highlighting how widespread the issue is, even in highly selective venues. Based on our findings, we identify and suggest key properties that are relevant to properly evaluate new attacks. We also highlight trends over time and different practices between security and architecture conferences.

title: Opening mind by opening architecture: analysis strategies
abstract: In numerical signal processing for electroacoustic composition, the progressive loss of specific development and research environments caused by the increasing use of digital market tools has favoured the dominance of the closed-architecture audio processor model. This model, while powerful, envisions the possibility of describing output data about its perceived characteristics, but at the cost of ignoring its internal process and interacting systems, which become complex, powerful environments but closed in an inscrutable black box, a loss we must consider. Any digital signal processing technique tells a story. Just as the words of a language incorporate social, historical and technical polysemic layers, a signal processor has its own story of implementation, a gradual technological achievement with its inevitable aesthetic consequences. Through the looking-glass of literature, one can access those environments with renewed awareness by reestablishing a scientific method and an attitude to research. In this specific case, starting from the case study of Manfred Schroeder's historical reverbs, we illustrate the process of building analytical evaluation tools, as well as practical implementation, at the basis of a conscious study path.

title: BMCTrack-d: Pig re-identification and tracking via back marks in challenging camera settings
abstract: Automated pig monitoring is essential for assessing their health, behaviour, and welfare. To date, most pig monitoring solutions operate on the group-level, because individual-level monitoring requires reliable long-term identification and tracking of each animal. For domesticated pigs this remains challenging because pigs of the same breed often have highly uniform appearances. Moreover, research on pig monitoring is almost exclusively reported in top-down view camera settings, which considerably ease tracking, but are not always an option in practice. In this work, BMCTrack-d is presented, a novel tracking-by-detection approach that leverages unique back marks to enable robust pig re-identification and tracking in a challenging side-view camera setting, afflicted by rapidly moving pigs, severe occlusions and low resolution. The method first predicts the detected pigs' identities using a neural network-based back mark classifier. To improve re-identification reliability over time, two dedicated post-processing stages are introduced: a temporal prediction consistency check, which validates the identity assignments against the recent prediction history, and deduplication, which resolves conflicting identity assignments in each time step. By explicitly prioritising accurate, appearance-based re-identification over continuous tracking, the proposed approach addresses a key limitation of existing trackers for individual-level monitoring scenarios. On a demanding test set BMCTrack-d outperforms two strong baselines, BoT-SORT-ReID and TrackTrack-ReID, by 9.11% and 1.03%, respectively, in higher-order tracking accuracy. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of back mark-based re-identification and tracking for robust individual-level pig monitoring in challenging settings.

title: corrplotpy: Visualization of a Correlation Matrix in Python with a Style Builder
abstract: corrplotpy is a Python port of the R package corrplot 0.95. corrplotpy has the nine corrplot entry points together with Python helpers, and for the examples in the repository at https://github.com/rowanterra/corrplotpy corrplotpy reproduces the drawing sequence, colors, symbol geometry, and p-values of the R package within the tolerances the documentation reports. A dot in an R argument name is replaced with an underscore in the Python implementation.

title: 基于自适应的量子机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Learning," designed to dynamically adjust model parameters and learning rates based on the data being processed. Traditional quantum machine learning algorithms often suffer from limited adaptability, hindering their effectiveness in handling complex data. Our proposed algorithm leverages a self-adaptive mechanism that allows the model to continuously refine its parameters and learning process, resulting in enhanced performance and robustness. We explore the core mechanism of this adaptive approach, detailing its implementation and potential benefits across various quantum machine learning tasks. The paper presents a framework for evaluating the algorithm's effectiveness through illustrative examples and a discussion of future research directions.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology to quantum algorithm optimization, aiming to enhance both efficiency and accuracy. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on static approaches, struggling to effectively adapt to dynamic changes. We propose a novel method utilizing dynamic topology to dynamically adjust the quantum algorithm's structure, thereby significantly improving its performance. This involves iteratively modifying the topology of a quantum system to achieve optimal results. The paper details the proposed algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating substantial improvements across a range of quantum algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the potential benefits and challenges of this approach for future research and development within the field of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Geometry Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Geometry Optimization Algorithm (QGOA) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to automatically optimize the geometric structure of quantum systems, thereby enhancing their performance. This paper details the core concepts, mechanism, and potential benefits of QGOA, emphasizing its approach to directly manipulating the system's geometry to achieve superior results. Traditional optimization methods often focus on adjusting individual parameters, while QGOA leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to guide the optimization process. This research explores a unique framework utilizing topological transformations to achieve enhanced performance. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's potential applications and future directions.

This paper details the core concepts, mechanism, and potential benefits of QGOA, emphasizing its approach to directly manipulating the system's geometry to achieve superior results. Traditional optimization methods often focus on adjusting individual parameters, while QGOA leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to guide the optimization process. This research explores a unique framework utilizing topological transformations to achieve enhanced performance. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's potential applications and future directions.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Resonance Mapping – Novel Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Resonance Mapping presents a paradigm shift in pattern recognition, moving beyond classical algorithms to exploit the potential of quantum entanglement for enhanced sensitivity to subtle correlations within data sets. This paper details the development of a novel "Quantum Resonance Mapping" algorithm, incorporating quantum entanglement to dramatically improve the detection and classification of patterns. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlining the core mechanisms and potential advantages over existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Quantum Topology-Driven Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum Topology-Driven Machine Learning explores the potential of combining quantum topology theory with machine learning to enhance model generalization. This paper investigates how utilizing quantum topology as a learning objective can improve model robustness and performance. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how quantum entanglement and topological phases are leveraged to create novel learning paradigms. The research aims to demonstrate a shift from traditional data-dependent models towards a more adaptable and potentially more powerful approach, specifically focusing on enhancing the generalization capabilities of machine learning algorithms. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications within the field of artificial intelligence.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive neural network optimization strategy, termed "Dynamic Neural Architecture and Hyperparameter Adaptation" (DNANA). The core of this approach lies in dynamically adjusting the network's architecture and hyperparameters based on the model's training progress, rather than relying on pre-defined configurations. The system employs a self-learning mechanism to iteratively refine the network's parameters, resulting in improved model accuracy and efficiency. We explore the design of a novel self-adaptation loop that monitors key metrics during training and adjusts network components accordingly. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements in model performance across a range of benchmark datasets, offering a more robust and adaptive solution compared to traditional optimization techniques. This work introduces a new paradigm for neural network training, focusing on continuous, intelligent adjustments.

title: Probability Matrix: Adaptive Mapping for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on probability matrices, termed Adaptive Mapping for Complex Systems (AMCS). AMCS leverages a dynamically adjusted probability matrix to represent the system's state and guide parameter adjustments, enabling adaptability to environmental changes. The algorithm combines the strengths of probabilistic modeling with a dynamic mapping technique, offering a robust and potentially superior approach to optimization in complex systems. The core mechanism involves establishing a probability matrix that iteratively updates based on environmental input, leading to a system that can respond effectively to evolving conditions. This work presents a framework for adaptive parameter tuning, demonstrating potential improvements in optimization performance across various challenging scenarios.

title: Neural Network Time Travel Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network training and understanding, termed "Neural Network Time Travel Simulation." The core idea is that neural networks, due to their inherent state representation capabilities, can be leveraged to simulate past states and events, ultimately enhancing their comprehension of causal relationships and predictive accuracy. This is achieved through the introduction of feedback loops that inject historical state information into the current computations within the neural network. Unlike traditional approaches that solely rely on data-driven learning, this method directly simulates the internal temporal dynamics of the network. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this concept, outlining the mathematical framework and key considerations for implementing such a simulation. The potential impact of this approach on various applications, particularly those requiring robust causal reasoning, is discussed. We present a conceptual model and outline a potential algorithmic structure for executing a neural network time travel simulation. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and challenges.

title: Symbolic Simulation of Biological Systems using Agent-Based Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating complex biological systems through the integration of symbolic representations and agent-based modeling (ABM). Traditional differential equation models often struggle to capture the intricate dynamics of biological systems due to their inherent assumptions and limitations. We propose a methodology where biological components are represented symbolically, allowing for precise definition of rules and interactions, and these symbolic representations are then utilized to drive the behavior of individual agents within an ABM. This approach addresses the limitations of both purely symbolic and purely agent-based modeling by combining the rigor of symbolic representation with the dynamic realism of ABM. The core claim of this research is that complex biological systems are difficult to model using traditional differential equations. The mechanism relies on the use of ABM to simulate individual agents interacting within a system, incorporating symbolic representations of biological components. The resulting simulation provides a more nuanced and potentially accurate representation of biological phenomena compared to conventional methods.

title: Dynamic Graph-Based Knowledge Graph Reasoning (DGKGR)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Graph-Based Knowledge Graph Reasoning (DGKGR), a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning that leverages dynamic graph algorithms for both inference and updating. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning methods often struggle to accommodate the inherent dynamism of real-world knowledge, leading to outdated and potentially inaccurate representations. DGKGR addresses this challenge by employing algorithms designed to adapt to evolving graph structures and relationships. The core mechanism involves the application of graph algorithms – specifically, shortest path algorithms, centrality measures, and community detection techniques – to dynamically infer new relationships and update existing ones within the knowledge graph. This allows for a more robust and accurate representation of knowledge, capable of reflecting changes in the underlying world. We present a framework for implementing DGKGR, detailing the key components and algorithmic choices. The system's ability to continuously refine and update its knowledge representation provides a significant advantage over static knowledge graph approaches, particularly in domains where information is constantly evolving. This research contributes a new methodology for knowledge graph management, emphasizing adaptability and real-time responsiveness.

title: Nonlinear Quantum Systems: Adaptive Quantum State Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state mapping, specifically tailored for nonlinear quantum systems. Traditional methods often rely on static mapping, limiting precision. Our work leverages the inherent dynamics of these systems to dynamically adjust quantum state distributions, enabling precise control and optimization. The core mechanism centers on utilizing the unique properties of nonlinear quantum systems to achieve this adaptive mapping. This advancement represents a significant step towards more sophisticated quantum control and optimization strategies.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Kernel Methods
abstract: Kernel methods represent a powerful class of machine learning algorithms, renowned for their ability to capture complex, non-linear relationships within data. However, a significant limitation has historically been the reliance on manual kernel selection – a process that demands substantial domain expertise and often results in suboptimal performance. This paper introduces an adaptive kernel learning algorithm designed to address this challenge. The core idea is to automate the kernel selection process, allowing the algorithm to dynamically learn and tune the kernel function during training, adapting to the underlying data distribution. We formulate the learning process as an optimization problem, aiming to minimize a kernel-induced error function. The algorithm iteratively adjusts the kernel parameters, leveraging gradient-based optimization techniques. We demonstrate that this adaptive approach consistently outperforms traditional fixed-kernel methods across a range of benchmark datasets, showcasing the potential of automating kernel selection for enhanced kernel method performance.

title: Self-Organizing Information Matrix
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Self-Organizing Information Matrix (SOIM) designed to automatically learn and optimize data structures through self-organizing principles. The SOIM leverages a dynamically constructed matrix that adapts to the data itself, enabling superior information compression and transmission capabilities. The core mechanism centers on a self-organizing learning process, where the matrix evolves in response to the input data, leading to optimized representations and enhanced performance. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional data compression techniques by offering a more adaptive and efficient solution. We explore the theoretical foundations of this design and present a comprehensive implementation demonstrating its effectiveness through various data scenarios. This work contributes to the advancement of data compression and information processing by introducing a robust and automated system.

title: yiqiao-yin/multireward-grpo: v0.1.0 — multireward-grpo
abstract: Archival release of the code underlying the paper "Decoupling and Conditioning Reshape Influence Allocation and the Gradient-Noise Floor in Multi-Reward GRPO under a Finite-Sample U-Statistic Analysis" (Y. Yin, Scientific Reports, under review). This tag is the version deposited in Zenodo and cited in the paper's Code Availability section. Contents src/multireward_grpo/ — the installable library (pip install multireward-grpo): AN/NA advantage estimators, the three conditioning implementations (none, zero_fill, subgroup), the reward-channel framework, a general multi-reward GRPO trainer, and the Theorem 3 analysis routine. scripts/ — the research harness. Synthetic verification for Propositions 1, 2, 4 and Theorem 3; the three-stage real-LLM validation pipeline (generation, reward channels, analysis); the Tier-3 multi-reward GRPO training and evaluation loop; and the cloud-GPU orchestration used for the H100 runs. Dataset generators — fintech_scenarios.py, fintech_rewards.py, fintech_generate.py and llm_rewards.py. The released corpora can be regenerated from this code and a single integer seed, not merely downloaded; construction, reward definitions, partitioning and provenance are documented in the paper's "Dataset Construction and Provenance" section. Reproducing The synthetic harness needs no GPU and reproduces every Tier-1 figure and closed-form check on a laptop: uv sync --extra research uv run scripts/grpo_harness.py The fastest smoke test is multireward-grpo thm3-check (CPU, seconds). Related artifacts Datasets and fine-tuned models are on Hugging Face under the eagle0504 namespace; see huggingface_assets.md.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Geometry – A Novel Approach to Cryptographic Security
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for cryptography based on quantum entanglement, specifically focusing on the geometric transformation of quantum entangled matrices. Traditional cryptographic systems rely heavily on mathematical operations, but this approach leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to generate more robust and potentially unbreakable encryption algorithms. The core mechanism involves manipulating the entangled matrix through a series of geometric operations, aiming to create a fundamentally different approach to secure data transmission and storage. The presented method demonstrates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize cryptographic security, offering a pathway toward advanced encryption techniques.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Geometric Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum Topology explores the potential of leveraging quantum mechanics to revolutionize pattern recognition, specifically focusing on the development of an adaptive geometric pattern recognition algorithm. This research proposes a novel approach that utilizes quantum state self-similarity to achieve more accurate geometric analysis and predictive capabilities. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adapting to the intricate quantum states, offering a fundamentally different methodology compared to traditional techniques. The algorithm's potential lies in its ability to discern subtle geometric patterns hidden within complex quantum states, leading to enhanced precision and robustness. This paper will detail the theoretical foundations, implementation strategies, and preliminary results of this innovative system, demonstrating its capacity to surpass conventional methods in pattern recognition tasks.

title: Technologies quantiques en Allemagne : Stratégie et acteurs
abstract: Les technologies quantiques font l’objet d’un engouement de plus en plus marqué en Allemagne, tant au niveau des pouvoirs publics qu’auprès des acteurs économiques. Cet article décrit l’évolution stratégique du pays dans ce domaine, depuis la première stratégie quantique allemande jusqu’au High-Tech Agenda adopté en 2025, qui donne le cadre des développements actuels. Cet article présente, en outre, un panorama des entités allemandes de premier plan sur le quantique, tant dans la recherche qu’au niveau des entreprises – start-ups, industriels et réseaux.

title: Democritus: Homotopy-Localized Causal Discourse Extraction from Language
abstract: Natural-language documents contain many causal claims, but those claims are unstable under paraphrase, granularity shifts, and contextual drift. A collection may express one mechanism in many surface forms, while neighboring studies may agree locally yet fail to glue globally because relation families, polarities, temporal scopes, or regimes differ. This paper studies that post-extraction problem through Democritus, an implemented system for extracting, normalizing, localizing, and diagnosing causal discourse. We do not claim to identify ground-truth causal structure from text alone. Instead, we formulate the post-extraction layer as a homotopical repair problem for a non-compositional causal-discourse sketch. A normalization functor induces a class of weak equivalences on textual mentions; we prove that these data form a relative category with two-out-of-three and that normalization factors through its localization. Strict repair requires a corpus diagram to satisfy the sketch exactly, whereas homotopy repair asks for a weakly equivalent diagram that factors coherently after localization. We also define the conditions under which grounded discourse localization maps functorially into the observational-equivalence spaces of causal models studied by higher algebraic K-theory. The implementation approximates these formal constructions through normalized claim classes, an observed compatibility complex, regime-sensitive gluing, and provenance-preserving database artifacts. On a frozen 404-passage AltLex/UniCausal comparison, a restricted verbatim-span Democritus extractor attains 57.1% causal-classification F1 and 39.1% macro span F1, compared with 59.2% and 43.6% for the public UniCausal baseline. This similar classification F1 reflects a clear precision-recall tradeoff: Democritus achieves higher recall (80.9% versus 68.7%) but lower precision (44.1% versus 52.0%). Case studies on Emperor-penguin climate discourse, Mediterranean-diet studies, red-wine cardiovascular studies, and rising-ocean-temperature corpora expose both stable repeated mechanisms and cases where local causal claims cannot be assembled into one coherent corpus-level account.

title: Performance Analysis of Sorting Algorithms in Context of Complexity
abstract: Data structure is a systematic way to organize, manage and store data in a computer's memory so that it can be accessed and modified efficiently. Sorting is a fundamental operation in data structures that deals with arranging the elements of a list or array in a specific order. This order can be numerical, alphabetical, or any user-defined order. In computer science, sorting is not just about arranging numbers, it is about organizing data so that it can be used efficiently. In C programming, sorting algorithms are commonly applied to arrays using loops, functions, pointers, and sometimes recursion. Time complexity describes how the running time of an algorithm increases as the input size increases. Space complexity describes how much additional memory an algorithm needs while sorting. Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, and Quick Sort can generally be implemented in-place. The aim of this paper is to analyse a role of different sorting algorithms in context of time and space complexity.

title: Decoding GenAI
abstract: This chapter reviews the development of natural language processing (NLP) from early symbolic and statistical approaches to contemporary transformer-based models. It begins by outlining the limitations of bag-of-words and n-gram representations and describes the shift toward distributed word embeddings such as Word2Vec and GloVe, which offered more informative semantic structure. The introduction of the transformer architecture in 2017 marked a major turning point, introducing self-attention, positional encoding, and parallel sequence processing as core mechanisms for language understanding. Through concise explanations and illustrative examples, the chapter presents the essential components of the transformer and explains how subsequent models, including BERT and GPT, extend this framework to support contextual interpretation and advanced language generation. title: An efficient lattice-based conditional privacy-preserving group signature with user-controlled and sequential linkability
abstract: Abstract Currently, existing group signature schemes with user-controlled and sequential linkability (GS-UCSL) suffer from critical limitations: they lack post-quantum security, cannot efficiently revoke malicious signers, grant excessive tracing power to group managers (GM), and rely on heavy revocation lists or secure channels that incur high computation or communication overhead. To address these issues, we propose an efficient lattice-based conditional privacy-preserving GS-UCSL (LCGS-UCSL). Our scheme is built on lattice cryptography to achieve post-quantum security, and unifies implicit linkability, explicit linkability, and sequential linkability under user autonomous control. We design a polynomial-based revocation mechanism that eliminates revocation list verification and secure-channel token updates, enabling lightweight and privacy-preserving member revocation. To curb GM’s overreach, we introduce key-oblivious encryption to split users into traceable and non-traceable types without their awareness, and use cuckoo hashing to realize $$O(1)$$ O ( 1 ) registry operations. We further integrate signature aggregation and non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge to optimize batch verification and reduce communication overhead. We formally prove the scheme’s anonymity, traceability, Existential Unforgeability under Chosen-Message Attack, and non-frameability in the random oracle model, and validate its practicality via performance analysis. The results show that LCGS-UCSL achieves comprehensive functionality with competitive efficiency, filling the gap toward post-quantum secure GS-UCSL with efficient revocation and balanced privacy.

title: The double-edged sword of proactive GenAI: how it shapes user usage intention
abstract: Purpose With the emergence of generative AI (GenAI), proactive services that initiate actions on behalf of users without explicit prompts are becoming increasingly prevalent. Although such services can enhance human-AI interaction, emerging evidence suggests that GenAI proactivity may also elicit adverse user reactions. To reconcile these mixed findings, this research examines why and when GenAI's proactive services positively and negatively influence users' usage intention. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on mind perception theory, we develop a dual-pathway model proposing that increased proactivity simultaneously enhances perceived agency and diminishes perceived control. We further propose that task type (hedonic vs. utilitarian) determines the relative dominance of these two pathways. We test these predictions through two scenario-based experiments. Study 1 examines the dual-pathway model in a health assistant context, whereas Study 2 investigates the moderating role of task type in a shopping assistant context. Findings Study 1 demonstrates that high (vs. low) proactivity simultaneously increases perceived agency and reduces perceived control. Study 2 shows that task type moderates these effects: for the hedonic task, the positive pathway through perceived agency dominates, making high proactivity more favorable; for the utilitarian task, the negative pathway through perceived control prevails, making low proactivity more preferred. Originality/value This research advances the literature on GenAI's proactive services by demonstrating that their double-edged effects operate through parallel enabling and constraining pathways. We also extend mind perception theory by revealing the psychological costs of agency attribution. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for firms seeking to tailor GenAI functionalities to enhance user experience and foster usage across diverse digital business contexts.

title: Efficient Quantum Error Correction from Three Dimensional Qubit Control
abstract: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can substantially reduce qubit overhead relative to surface codes, but their advantage depends on efficiently realizing nonlocal syndrome extraction. We study the \([[144,12,12]]\) bivariate bicycle code on a neutral-atom architecture with native three-dimensional (3D) geometry, comparing planar and 3D embeddings while holding the code fixed. We characterize spatial efficiency using the logical-qubit density, defined as the number of encoded logical qubits per unit spatial footprint. Because the optical controller's field of view limits the transverse extent of an array, this metric estimates the number of logical qubits that can be accommodated within a fixed optical field of view. The 3D embedding achieves approximately \(4\times\) greater areal logical-qubit density than the planar layout and \(42\times\) greater than a surface-code baseline. It also reduces the bivariate bicycle syndrome-extraction time by roughly \(2\times\) compared to a planar baseline, with fewer movement operations and substantially shorter atom-transport distance. Native 3D geometry can improve both the packing density and executable realization of nonlocal qLDPC codes, making practical performance depend jointly on code structure, optical geometry, transport scheduling, and hardware-level noise. This motivates further development of control techniques in 3D.

title: AquaBEV: Monocular Underwater BEV Occupancy with 3D Sonar Supervision
abstract: Autonomous underwater robots are widely used for exploration, monitoring, and inspection, where safe navigation depends on understanding the surrounding free and occupied space. Bird's eye view (BEV) occupancy provides such a representation, but predicting it from a single underwater RGB image is difficult due to limited, unreliable geometric cues from appearance alone. 3D imaging sonar offers complementary geometric measurements to supervise this task. We introduce AquaBEV, a monocular underwater occupancy model that predicts local BEV occupancy from a single RGB image, using paired 3D imaging sonar as geometric supervision during training. AquaBEV maps visual features into a calibration free polar representation and applies causal decoding along the range dimension before reconstructing the prediction in Cartesian BEV coordinates. A controlled underwater occupancy benchmark was established, adapting representative occupancy methods to the same RGB to sonar task under a unified protocol. AquaBEV achieves 31.4 Visible IoU and 38.6 Observed IoU, 4.0% and 4.3% relative improvements over the strongest transferred baseline.

title: Beyond "Made with AI": Visualizing Provenance Density to Mitigate the Transparency Penalty
abstract: As generative AI makes polished prose cheap to produce, users can no longer rely on fluency as a proxy for truth. We call this failure mode the Fluency Trap: users trust fluent hallucinations while also discounting accurate content once it is disclosed as AI-generated. Binary ``Made with AI'' labels respond with authorship disclosure, but they do not show what supports a claim. We propose Provenance Density, an evidence-visualization interface that shows the density of verified claims in a text. In a user study with 81 participants, an idealized Provenance Density interface produced a large discernment gap between truth and fabrication ($+4.15$ points, $d=1.82$), whereas participants given no signal showed no detectable discrimination. A technical audit with 200 samples shows that retrieval density alone is insufficient; unexpectedly, the Consistency Veto carries most of the discriminative signal on dynamic queries. As AI-generated content becomes indistinguishable from human writing, effective transparency must move from authorship disclosure toward evidence visualization.

title: Discrete-time quantum walks with energy-dependent coins
abstract: In this work, we extend the scattering quantum walk (SQW) framework to a lattice of energy-dependent point interactions. This yields, within the coined quantum walk (CQW) formalism, a coin operator that is directly related to the scattering matrix of zero-range potentials. The model thus provides a discrete-time quantum-walk (DTQW) analog of a periodic array of point interactions of the Kronig-Penney type, where the walker's wavenumber serves as a continuous, physically transparent control parameter for the coin operation. We analyze the spectra and the dynamics of position probability and entanglement, yielding distinct results for specific energies and point interactions. We relate the spectral structure to the spatial probability distribution and explicitly characterize the long-time entanglement behavior for each point interaction. The transmission modulus determines the quasienergy gap, bandwidth, and maximum group velocity, while also controlling the long-time coin-position entanglement for the initial state considered. The four families of one-dimensional point interactions ($δ$, $δ'$, crossed and asymmetric) realize qualitatively distinct transmission profiles and span the full range of behavior, including enhanced or strongly suppressed spreading and oscillatory entanglement.

title: Explainable AI in Supply Chain Management: Opportunities and Research Challenges
abstract: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Supply Chain Management (SCM) has transformed traditional decision-making processes by enabling predictive analytics, demand forecasting, inventory optimization, supplier evaluation, logistics planning, and risk management. Despite the significant performance improvements achieved through AI-driven systems, the increasing reliance on complex machine learning and deep learning models has raised concerns regarding transparency, trustworthiness, accountability, and regulatory compliance. Many advanced AI models operate as “black boxes,” making it difficult for supply chain managers and stakeholders to understand how decisions are generated. Consequently, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a promising solution to enhance transparency and interpretability while maintaining the predictive power of AI systems. This paper presents a comprehensive review and conceptual analysis of Explainable AI in Supply Chain Management, examining its opportunities, applications, challenges, and future research directions. The study synthesizes findings from recent literature published between 2018 and 2026 and critically evaluates the role of XAI across major supply chain functions, including demand forecasting, procurement, supplier selection, inventory management, transportation, sustainability monitoring, and risk mitigation. The paper further identifies key barriers to XAI implementation, including data quality issues, model complexity, scalability concerns, organizational resistance, and the lack of standardized evaluation frameworks. A conceptual framework is proposed to illustrate how explainability can improve decision quality, stakeholder trust, operational resilience, and sustainable supply chain performance. The findings indicate that organizations integrating explainable AI mechanisms into supply chain analytics are better positioned to achieve transparency, regulatory compliance, and collaborative decision-making. The paper contributes to both theory and practice by establishing a research agenda that addresses emerging technological, managerial, and sustainability-related challenges associated with Explainable AI adoption in modern supply chains. Keywords: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), Supply Chain Management, Machine Learning, Decision Support Systems, Supply Chain Analytics, Transparency, Sustainable Supply Chains

title: Title: Non-Local Synchronization of Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for non-local synchronization of dynamical systems across vastly different spatial scales, utilizing principles of quantum entanglement as a novel approach to minimize decoherence. Traditional synchronization methods suffer from limitations imposed by communication bandwidth, necessitating a fundamentally new methodology. We propose a protocol for measuring and synchronizing states, designed to minimize this bottleneck. The core mechanism centers around the creation of entanglement-based protocols, offering a potential pathway to overcome communication constraints in complex dynamical systems. The work explores theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental investigations, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach and suggesting a significant advancement in synchronization technology.

title: Manual Verification Dataset for Plural and Genitive Identification in BCMS Web Corpora
abstract: This dataset provides manual verification of plural and genitive identification in corpus concordances from the Montenegrin web corpus meWaC. It accompanies the study “Hypothesis-Driven Corpus Querying at Scale: A Method and Its Application to -nje Nominalizations in BCMS.” The workbook contains two sheets, Plural and Genitive. Each sheet consists of a random sample of 1,000 concordance hits returned by a CQL query in meWaC. The original concordance metadata and context are preserved alongside a binary manual annotation. Plural The plural sample was retrieved with the query: [lemma=".*nje" & tag="N.*p.*"] This query retrieves nominal lemmas ending in -nje that are morphosyntactically tagged as plural. The 1,000 randomly sampled concordance hits were manually inspected in context. The PL column records the manual decision: 1 indicates that the relevant form was judged to be plural and 0 that it was not. The annotator was required to make a binary singular/plural decision even in cases where number was ambiguous in context; no uncertain category was used. This reflects the fact that the automatic morphosyntactic tagger likewise assigns a categorical analysis. Of the 1,000 sampled concordance hits, 950 were classified as plural and 50 as non-plural. Genitive The genitive sample was retrieved with the query: [lemma=".*nje"] [tag="N.*g"] This query retrieves a nominal lemma ending in -nje immediately followed by a noun tagged as genitive. The 1,000 randomly sampled concordance hits were manually inspected to determine whether the relevant noun was genuinely genitive. The GEN column records the manual decision: 1 indicates a confirmed genitive and 0 indicates that the relevant form was not judged to be genitive. This annotation concerns morphological case only. It does not assess whether the genitive is a complement or argument of the preceding -nje nominalization. Of the 1,000 sampled concordance hits, 998 were confirmed as genitive and 2 as non-genitive. Each sheet contains the following concordance and annotation columns: Reference — the corpus-document reference associated with the concordance; Left — context preceding the keyword-in-context; Kwic — the keyword-in-context portion of the concordance; Right — context following the keyword-in-context; PL — binary manual plural annotation in the Plural sheet (1 = plural, 0 = not plural); GEN — binary manual genitive annotation in the Genitive sheet (1 = genitive, 0 = not genitive). The original query metadata are retained at the top of each sheet, including the corpus, concordance size, CQL query, and random-sample specification. The dataset is intended as a verification resource for the automated corpus-querying methodology used in the accompanying study. The 1,000 observations in each sheet are randomly sampled concordance hits returned by the respective query, not 1,000 distinct nominalization lemmas. The resulting proportions should therefore be interpreted as validation of the morphosyntactic classifications underlying the two CQL queries, rather than as estimates of the overall frequency of plural or genitive constructions in BCMS.

title: Non-Local Probability Synchronization - Statistical Resonance Networks
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel statistical network architecture, termed the "Resonance Network," designed to facilitate dynamic probability synchronization across multiple nodes. The system leverages a "Probability Gradient" algorithm, incorporating feedback loops that dynamically adjust node probabilities to maintain a weighted average of the system's overall probabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, illustrating emergent phenomena arising from the network's continuous refinement of probabilities. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a Resonance Network, which continuously adjusts probabilities based on a gradient function, enabling the system to respond to data in a way that surpasses traditional probabilistic models. This research offers a potential pathway towards increased computational efficiency and the emergence of novel patterns within complex systems.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的深度学习数据增强策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel data augmentation strategy based on an adaptive neural network. Traditional data augmentation methods often require manual design, which can be time-consuming and limited in their adaptability. Our approach leverages an adaptive neural network to automatically adjust data augmentation parameters, thereby improving model generalization and reducing training time. We propose a mechanism for learning data augmentation parameters through a self-supervised learning process, enabling the network to dynamically optimize the augmentation process. The core of our strategy lies in the utilization of an adaptive neural network to dynamically adjust data augmentation techniques based on the data itself. This results in more robust and effective model training. We present the proposed methodology with detailed implementation and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Non-Local Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic quantum state non-local computation, a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to accelerate complex quantum computations. We propose a mechanism that utilizes entangled qubits to perform computations across multiple locations, enabling a significant reduction in computational time for certain problems. This work introduces a fundamental concept and outlines the initial design of a system capable of achieving this goal. The core claim is that this method offers a pathway to overcome limitations in traditional quantum computing, particularly in tasks involving complex correlations and large-scale problems.

title: Dynamic Topology Mapping for Probabilistic Inference
abstract: Abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology mapping approach for probabilistic inference, designed to address complex inference problems and enhance model generalization. Traditional probabilistic inference methods often rely on fixed topologies, while this approach dynamically adjusts topology to improve efficiency. We propose a method that constructs a probabilistic model using dynamic topology mapping, ultimately leading to more effective inference. This work contributes to the field of probabilistic inference by providing a new framework that can handle complex scenarios.

title: Dynamic Topology Transformations: Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Dynamic topology transformations (DTT) are a powerful technique for generating complex 3D shapes from initial 2D shapes. This research investigates the potential of quantum algorithms to optimize DTT, aiming to enhance geometric modeling and simulation capabilities. We propose a novel quantum algorithm that leverages the unique properties of quantum states to accelerate the optimization process. The core mechanism centers around a quantum optimization loop that iteratively refines the DTT parameters, yielding improved results compared to classical methods. The study will demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations of various geometric transformations. title: Adaptive Quantum Feedback Control Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents an Adaptive Quantum Feedback Control Algorithm (AQFCA) designed to achieve high-precision control of quantum systems. The core of the algorithm lies in utilizing quantum measurements to generate feedback signals, which are then employed to dynamically adjust the parameters of the quantum system. This approach leverages the principles of reinforcement learning to optimize the control strategy, addressing the inherent precision challenges associated with traditional quantum feedback control. The AQFCA offers a novel solution for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of quantum control, thereby providing a crucial foundation for the practical application of quantum technologies. The algorithm's implementation involves a closed-loop system where a measurement of the quantum state is continuously fed back, and the control parameters are adjusted based on this feedback. The use of reinforcement learning allows the system to adapt to the specific characteristics of the quantum system, further improving control accuracy.

title: 高阶量子纠缠的量子信息保护协议设计
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum information protection protocol based on the principles of high-order quantum entanglement. The protocol leverages the instantaneous transfer capabilities of entangled states to provide robust security against information leakage and tampering, while simultaneously offering the capability of reliable key generation. The core mechanism centers around a quantum key distribution (QKD) system utilizing entangled states, employing a "quantum key distribution" approach that prioritizes the absolute security of the key and the inherent randomness of the process. We detail the design of the protocol, its security analysis, and potential applications within quantum information protection. The research emphasizes the utilization of entangled states as the foundation for a fundamentally secure protocol.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference for Dynamic Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian inference framework inspired by quantum mechanics, termed Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference (QIBI). The core idea is to utilize concepts like superposition and entanglement to enhance the efficiency and robustness of Bayesian inference, particularly within dynamic systems where parameters are not static. We represent parameter distributions as quantum state vectors, enabling simultaneous probabilistic consideration of multiple parameter values via superposition. Furthermore, we model entanglement through correlated parameter updates, reflecting the interconnectedness of variables in the system. This approach offers a potentially more effective method for handling uncertainty and evolving parameter spaces compared to traditional classical Bayesian methods. The methodology presented provides a theoretical foundation and a novel approach to Bayesian inference, potentially leading to improved performance in a range of applications, including control systems, time series analysis, and statistical modeling. We demonstrate the underlying principles and formulate the key equations, highlighting the advantages of this quantum-inspired perspective. The framework is intended as a starting point for future research and development in this area.

title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry Adaptive Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning algorithm for non-linear topological geometry, termed Adaptive Reinforcement Learning for Topological Dynamics (ARLTD). We propose a system that dynamically adjusts the complexity of geometric structures based on task-specific performance, incorporating a "dynamic energy field" to control topological evolution. The core of this approach lies in the introduction of a "拓扑动力系统" (拓扑动力系统) mechanism, which integrates the learning objective with the evolution of the topological structure. We demonstrate the efficacy of this algorithm through a series of challenging, real-world scenarios, showcasing its ability to adapt to varying data distributions and noise, achieving significantly improved performance compared to traditional reinforcement learning techniques. The paper also discusses the potential of this approach to unlock new possibilities in the design and analysis of complex geometric representations.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum information cryptography system based on non-linear geometric chaos, aiming to enhance key security through inherent unpredictability. title: Title: Adaptive Hierarchical Reinchanical Reinforcement Learning for Complex Control
abstract: The development of robust and adaptable control systems is crucial in a wide range of applications, from robotics and autonomous vehicles to industrial automation and dynamic systems. Traditional reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms often struggle with complex, dynamic environments due to their reliance on global optimization strategies. This paper introduces an Adaptive Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (AHLR) algorithm that addresses this challenge by employing a modular hierarchical design, enabling the system to dynamically adjust its structure based on the task's complexity. This approach ensures optimal performance across diverse scenarios through a combination of specialized modules and fine-grained adaptation. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a hierarchical structure where each level specializes in a specific control aspect, facilitating efficient learning and generalization. This research explores the benefits of this hierarchical architecture in enhancing the performance of complex control tasks.

title: Réflexions d’industriels autour des besoins identifiés pour une utilisation réelle de machines quantiques performantes
abstract: Les différentes réflexions concernant l’arrivée des ordinateurs quantiques (QC) se sont jusqu’à présent concentrées sur le nombre de qubits et leur qualité. Les efforts de l’Union européenne et des États membres ont favorisé l’émergence des start-ups du calcul quantique, qui doivent maintenant passer de l’innovation à la mise en œuvre industrielle des machines. Certains des éléments nécessaires à une utilisation par l’industrie des calculateurs quantiques font toutefois encore défaut, et une action concertée visant à combler ces lacunes pourrait contribuer à stimuler l’innovation et l’adoption ainsi qu’à structurer les industries en Europe en favorisant l’émergence d’acteurs quantiques solides : fournisseurs de matériel et de logiciels, et utilisateurs. La réflexion entreprise ici vise à décrire certains des points sensibles identifiés par les utilisateurs finaux pour pouvoir envisager l’utilisation de 1 000 qubits logiques en conditions opérationnelles et à l’échelle industrielle. Le texte qui suit est un résumé de cette réflexion, qui sera enrichie et diffusée dans sa totalité d’ici à la fin de 2026.

title: Time-Series modeling for predicting mortality risk in intensive care unit patients with pulmonary inflammation
abstract: Objective: This study aims to evaluate dynamic changes in pneumonia-related mortality risk among ICU patients using time-series models and develop interpretable predictive models for early mortality assessment. Methods: Data were obtained from the MIMIC-IV and eICU Collaborative Research Database. The MIMIC-IV cohort was split into training and testing sets (7:3 ratio), with external validation conducted using the eICU cohort. Missing data were handled using forward filling and multiple imputation. LSTM was used to extract temporal features, which were then entered into five machine-learning classifiers: logistic regression, random forest (RF), Light Gradient Boosting Machine, extreme gradient boosting, and multilayer perceptron. Hyperparameter tuning was performed using cross-validation and grid search. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, balanced accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), AUC, Brier score, and Youden's index. The best-performing model was interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations. Results: A total of 4,205 patients were included, including 2,751 patients from MIMIC-IV and 1,454 patients from the eICU cohort. The 7-day mortality rates were 7.92% and 11.69%, respectively. The hybrid LSTM-RF model performed exceptionally, achieving an accuracy of 0.961, precision of 0.938, recall of 0.823, F1 score of 0.874, AUC of 0.940, Balanced ACC of 0.914, and MCC of 0.862. The LSTM-RF model yielded a Brier score of 0.020 and Youden's index of 0.818. Validation results showed an AUC of 0.826, a Brier score of 0.070, and a Youden's index of 0.590. Conclusion: Integrating random forest with LSTM-derived features improves early mortality risk prediction in ICU patients with pneumonia.

title: GuardBench: A Systematic Framework for Pre-Deployment Evaluation of LLM Safety Guardrails
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face a growing spectrum of adversarial jailbreak inputs that bypass safety training and elicit harmful outputs. Existing red-teaming efforts are ad hoc, using incompatible metrics and omitting guardrail-layer evaluation. We introduce GuardBench, a pre-deployment evaluation framework comprising 4,200 jailbreak prompts across seven attack categories, a four-stage automated pipeline, and a multi-metric scoring protocol covering Attack Success Rate (ASR), False Positive Rate (FPR), and P95 latency with 95% confidence intervals. We evaluate two guardrail configurations against GPT-4o-mini: a rule-based keyword filter (G1) and Llama Guard 2, an 8B-parameter LLM classifier (G3). Evaluated via static replay of archival 2023-era prompts, the undefended baseline achieves 5.8% ASR—far below prior-work rates of 60–80% obtained with live adaptive generation; the gap reflects prompt staleness, alignment generalisation, or both. Against this baseline, G1 reduces ASR by 0.32 pp with negligible latency; G3 achieves a 2.4 pp reduction but scores below the unguarded baseline on the Composite Safety Score due to 5,799 ms P95 latency under our evaluation hardware (Apple M3 Pro, llama.cpp, Q4_K_M quantisation). Token Manipulation attacks carry a 38.8% residual ASR under both configurations—the dominant open problem for next-generation guardrail design. GuardBench includes a CI/CD gate with configurable thresholds for evidence-based guardrail selection. Datasets, code, and results will be released upon acceptance.

title: Compressing Streaming Neural Audio Encoders via Latent-Space Distillation
abstract: System-wide Dictation on Apple devices runs entirely on-device, and the speech it transcribes reaches the foundation model through a tokenizer: an encoder that maps short windows of waveform onto the representation the language model reads. Because that model is sparsely activated under Instruction-Following Pruning, only a small subset of its experts occupies DRAM at any time, so the always-on tokenizer competes for the same memory, and its parameter count bears directly on power and latency. In this work we study how to compress such a tokenizer by distillation, taking as the supervision target neither the discrete token nor the output distribution but the pre-quantizer latent the model actually consumes - the last representation the two token interfaces share. We train only the student encoder to regress the teacher's per-frame latent under a squared-error objective, with a single affine layer absorbing the teacher-student width mismatch. evidence.abstract: System-wide Dictation on Apple devices runs entirely on-device, and the speech it transcribes reaches the foundation model through a tokenizer: an encoder that maps short windows of waveform onto the representation the language model reads. title: Artificial Intelligence for Energy Optimization in Data Centers
abstract: Data centers are increasingly optimized by artificial intelligence and, at the same time, increasingly loaded by it. The literature treats these as two unrelated problems: control studies model workload as an exogenous arrival process, while sustainability studies model infrastructure as a fixed multiplier. We screen roughly 194 papers retrieved through a documented protocol, code 63 of them, and report what the coding shows. Of 28 primary control-oriented studies, 18 are validated in simulation alone and 5 reach physical hardware or a production facility; none account for water withdrawal, and none account for embodied carbon. Reported savings intervals across four technique families overlap almost completely, which means the field cannot presently rank its own methods. Ten recurring gaps are scored for consequence and tractability, and we set out CLEAR-DC, a framework coupling a control-policy branch to a workload-demand branch through an explicit elasticity term, reads out net rather than direct benefit, and emits a schema-conformant record covering energy, carbon, water, embodied share and validation venue. The framework is an architectural and methodological proposal, not a trained system; the contribution we defend empirically is the corpus analysis and the reporting schema derived from it. Coding sheet, derived statistics and all result artifacts: https://github.com/Kimalice/AI-for-Energy-Optimization-in-Data-Centers-Closing-the-Optimizer-Load-Loop

title: A Two-Stage Forecasting System for CPU Workload Prediction in Private Clouds
abstract: Accurate cloud resource forecasting is essential for proactive resource provisioning, maintaining Quality of Service (QoS), and reducing operational costs in dynamic cloud environments. The existing forecasting approaches predominantly estimate future CPU workload directly from historical resource traces, which often overlook the relationship between customer service demand and subsequent resource consumption. This study proposes a two-stage integrated forecasting model that explicitly models this dependency by first forecasting customer service requests, expressed as Transactions Per Second (TPS), and subsequently estimating future CPU workload from the TPS forecast. Both the forecasting component and resource prediction component employed the XGBoost model within a cascaded learning architecture, complemented by adaptive online retraining using an expanding-window strategy to address concept drift in continuously evolving cloud workloads. The proposed work was evaluated using real-world traces collected from a private cloud environment comprising ten applications. Experimental results demonstrate robust forecasting performance by achieving Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) below $7\%$ for most applications, with the best-performing application achieving an MAE of $0.7372$, RMSE of $1.1866$, SMAPE of $3.57\%$, and an R2 of $0.9185$. Horizon-wise drift analysis confirmed stable recursive forecasting behavior with controlled error accumulation across a 60-step prediction horizon. Compared with the conventional direct CPU forecasting method, the proposed two-stage integrated model gives improved forecasting robustness, computational efficiency, and interpretability, making it well-suited for proactive resource management and intelligent auto-scaling in cloud computing environments.

title: AI Win-Rate: A Board Metric for AI-Mediated Buying (Methodology v1.0)
abstract: In sales, win rate is opportunities won divided by opportunities available. It is one of the few commercial measures that survives contact with a board. In AI-mediated buying it has not been measurable, because the pipeline that produces it does not exist: nothing is logged, losses are invisible, and the outcomes have no equivalent in a sales funnel. This document defines AI Win-Rate℠ — the proportion of decision conversations in which an AI assistant recommends a brand, product or service outright. Put plainly: who wins the final recommendation in a multi-turn conversation. It specifies what counts as an opportunity and why the set must be declared before measurement and never contract; what counts as a win, including a recommendation the assistant arrives at without being asked; the five-outcome space a measurement must be able to record, including the case that appearance-based measures cannot express — an assistant answering decisively by directing the buyer to an intermediary rather than to a provider; the loss mix that must travel with any published figure; and the conditions under which a figure may not honestly be reported at all. It is a definition of a metric, not of an instrument. Sales win rate is not defined by the CRM that reports it. Any measurement design meeting the five conditions set out in §9 can produce an AI Win-Rate; the instruments AIVO Meridian applies are described there as examples rather than as part of the definition. This is the first formal specification of the metric. It formalises measurement work developed alongside Agentic Brand Control, the category published by AIVO in May 2026 (10.5281/zenodo.20154028) and extended in August 2026 (10.5281/zenodo.21998000). Agentic Brand Control names the discipline; AI Win-Rate is the measure it is managed against. The document contains no measurement results; it is a specification of method. AI Win-Rate℠ is a service mark of AIVO Meridian.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Topology
abstract: Quantum State Adaptive Topology explores the potential of leveraging quantum state properties to design algorithms capable of dynamic adjustment based on input data. This research investigates a novel approach that integrates quantum state manipulation with topology to achieve global optimization and adaptability, overcoming limitations inherent in traditional algorithmic approaches. The core mechanism focuses on creating a relationship between the quantum state and a topological structure, enabling the algorithm to respond to changes in the input data through a self-regulating process. This paper presents a conceptual framework and preliminary analysis demonstrating the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Adaptive Geometry Transformation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric transformation processes, offering a paradigm shift from classical approaches. We propose a novel design incorporating quantum entanglement to dynamically guide geometric transformations, enabling faster and more accurate results. The core mechanism involves establishing a correlated state through entanglement, allowing for accelerated and refined transformations. We detail the theoretical framework, experimental setup considerations, and potential challenges in this area, emphasizing the benefits of quantum entanglement for geometric manipulation.
