title: Candidate Comparability Before Promotion: Conditional Validation in Adaptive Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: Adaptive network intrusion detection systems retrain classifiers after drift alarms, but an alarm detects change; it does not establish that a challenger should replace the deployed incumbent. Promotion is security-relevant because it changes the model responsible for subsequent attack detection, and evaluating it has a methodological problem: promotion conclusions may depend on how the challenger was constructed and on how much evidence supports it. We test that dependence on CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15 and ToN-IoT with self-contained challenger pipelines, nested candidate-size controls, a common-harness comparison of nine update policies, and a final sensitivity confining every exact feature vector to one evaluation, training or probe role. Incumbent-owned frozen preprocessing amplified apparent promotion harm; with self-contained challenger pipelines the mean full-drift harm did not persist. Raising nominal candidate evidence from 512 to 2,000 samples per class improved promotion under pool-constructed progressive drift by +0.53, +1.67 and +0.38 balanced-accuracy points: positive and statistically resolved in all three benchmarks, but materially benchmark-dependent rather than homogeneous, and driven mainly by fewer false positives. Policy conclusions were partially robust: policy ordering changed with candidate comparability, no policy globally dominated, and earlier compatibility statements for a label-free estimator and a calibrated ensemble narrowed. Validation helped evidence-disadvantaged challengers but added no average benefit at parity. Thirteen replays on real, time-ordered traffic showed no net harm from always deploying. Challenger construction and evidence should be controlled, reported and interpreted explicitly when promotion is evaluated.

title: STARS-GS: Structure-Aware Regularized Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Aerial Surface Reconstruction
abstract: Large-scale 3D surface reconstruction from aerial imagery is fundamental to geospatial mapping and urban modeling. Recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have demonstrated considerable potential for this task. However, existing methods still face three major challenges in large and complex scenes: scene partitioning may split continuous scene elements across independently optimized sub-regions; geometric constraints mainly focus on the attributes of individual Gaussians while overlooking their local organization; and uniform regularization struggles to accommodate heterogeneous geometric structures. To address these issues, we propose STARS-GS, a structure-aware 3DGS framework for large-scale surface reconstruction. First, we introduce a structure-aware scene partitioning strategy that better preserves continuous scene structures during partitioning and reduces cross-region geometric inconsistencies and stitching artifacts through boundary refinement. Second, we develop neighborhood-aware Gaussian organization that extends geometric constraints from individual primitives to their neighborhood organization, encouraging Gaussians to better conform to local surface geometry. Third, we introduce adaptive surface regularization that adjusts the regularization strength according to local geometric characteristics, promoting geometric consistency in structured regions while preserving plausible variations in unstructured regions. Extensive experiments on large-scale aerial photogrammetry benchmarks demonstrate that STARS-GS consistently outperforms the evaluated Gaussian-based methods in surface reconstruction. It increases the average F1-score from 0.640 for the second-best method to 0.698, corresponding to a relative improvement of approximately 9.1\%, demonstrating effective improvements in geometric accuracy and surface completeness.

title: PACodec: A Low-bitrate Neural Speech Codec with Parallel Additive Vector Quantization
abstract: This paper proposes PACodec, a novel low-bitrate neural speech codec based on parallel additive vector quantization (PAVQ). Unlike the mainstream residual vector quantization (RVQ) used in most neural speech codecs, where vector quantizers (VQs) are sequentially dependent, the PAVQ strategy adopted in PACodec aggregates parallel quantization results to optimize bitrate usage. Specifically, the PAVQ adopts a "global-local-global" (GLG) design: the global encoded features are quantized in parallel by multiple independent VQs, each attending to a local component of the representation, and their outputs are aggregated through addition to yield the final global quantization result for decoding. Experimental results show that PACodec, as each VQ focuses only on local information, supports smaller codebooks and reduces bitrate by 30% compared with baselines at the same decoding quality, with only minor model complexity. Further analysis shows that, owing to the GLG framework of PAVQ, the proposed PACodec is disentanglement-friendly, and each independent VQ captures different aspects of speech, e.g., content, timbre, and acoustic details, suggesting potential for application to downstream tasks such as voice conversion.

title: LAR-OS: Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Operating System & Unified Antigravity Gateway
abstract: LAR-OS (Language Agent Research Operating System) v3.0.0 is an open-source, enterprise-grade autonomous multi-agent engineering operating system and unified AI gateway. Core Capabilities: Bidirectional Anthropic ↔ Gemini Tool-Calling Translation: Enables Claude Code CLI and Anthropic-native tools to execute multi-step autonomous loops through Google Gemini 2.5 Flash / Pro engines with zero code changes. Antigravity ↔ Jules Multi-Agent Delegation: Implements a strict hierarchical orchestration architecture (User → Antigravity Chief Orchestrator → Jules Delegated Worker Pool → GitHub / Hugging Face Source of Truth) with automated code review under Anti-Crash Protocol (ACP-V1). Distributed Multi-Node Compute: Pools multi-account Google AI Pro credentials and SSH Linux Cloud Shell nodes with dynamic round-robin failover and smart cooldown. RTK Context Compactor & Bounded LRU Cache: Reduces token overhead by 35% and accelerates prompt turnaround time while protecting against memory exhaustion. Continuous Knowledge Sync: Automated bi-directional synchronization across Google Drive for PC, Obsidian Vault, and NotebookLM.

title: Dynamic Graph Theory-based Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic graph theory-based optimization algorithm designed to improve the speed and quality of optimization processes. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static graph structures, which can limit the algorithm's effectiveness. We propose a method that dynamically modifies the graph structure during the optimization process, creating a more efficient representation of the problem. This adaptation allows the algorithm to effectively navigate complex landscapes and find optimal solutions more rapidly. The core mechanism involves analyzing the problem's structure and adjusting the graph to enhance connectivity and reduce the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and illustrative examples, showcasing significant improvements in solution speed and quality compared to existing optimization techniques.

title: Quantum Topology for Quantum Computing Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a novel field of physics, offers a unique approach to manipulating quantum states and exploring complex quantum phenomena. This paper explores the potential of quantum topology to revolutionize algorithm optimization within the realm of quantum computing. We propose a new algorithmic framework, 'Quantum Topology Optimization', predicated on the principles of quantum topology to enhance the efficiency and performance of various quantum algorithms. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to guide the optimization process, leading to significant improvements in computational outcomes. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings, implementation considerations, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach. We conclude with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: 自适应时空几何的量子模拟验证
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive spacetime geometry in quantum simulation verification. Traditional quantum simulation validation often relies on static parameter adjustments, limiting accuracy and efficiency. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts simulation parameters based on the results of the simulation, leading to improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism involves utilizing self-adaptive spacetime geometry to iteratively refine the simulation's parameters, optimizing for verification accuracy. This approach addresses the limitations of static validation methods by providing a continuous feedback loop. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a series of simulations focusing on verifying the properties of a simplified quantum system. The study highlights the potential of this approach to significantly enhance the reliability and speed of quantum simulation verification.

title: 基于自适应的梯度下降算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel gradient descent algorithm, termed "Adaptive Gradient Descent" (AGD), designed to enhance convergence speed and robustness. Traditional gradient descent frequently operates on a uniform learning rate and momentum, leading to suboptimal optimization and susceptibility to local minima. AGD dynamically adjusts the learning rate and momentum based on the local gradient landscape, intelligently prioritizing areas with higher curvature and minimizing the risk of getting stuck in suboptimal solutions. This paper details the algorithm's core mechanism, including the gradient landscape adaptation process and its resulting benefits in terms of faster convergence and improved robustness. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance on various benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superior results compared to established gradient descent methods.

title: Quantum Privacy via Entanglement Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates the utilization of entanglement decoherence as a novel privacy-preserving mechanism within quantum computation. The core concept hinges on strategically introducing controlled decoherence into quantum calculations, thereby mitigating the risk of information leakage and facilitating secure quantum processing. Traditional approaches to quantum privacy often rely on complex cryptographic protocols, which can introduce significant overhead and limitations. This research proposes a fundamentally different method leveraging the inherent properties of entanglement and its susceptibility to decoherence. Specifically, we explore techniques for introducing precisely calibrated decoherence effects to obscure the intermediate quantum states, effectively limiting the information accessible to potential eavesdroppers. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key mathematical relationships and operational considerations for achieving this goal, focusing on the probabilistic reduction of information leakage. The proposed model offers a potentially more efficient and scalable approach to quantum privacy, addressing some of the challenges associated with existing solutions. We define key parameters such as decoherence rate (Γ), initial entanglement fidelity (F₀), and the degree of controlled decoherence (δ) to quantify the effectiveness of the privacy protection. The work culminates in a discussion of the trade-offs between privacy and computational utility, highlighting the need for careful parameter optimization.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Simulation of Non-Linear Systems
abstract: Quantum-enhanced geometric simulation aims to revolutionize the modeling of complex, non-linear systems by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to stabilize and improve the accuracy of geometric simulations, addressing key challenges in current computational methods. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm designed to enhance the fidelity of geometric representations, offering a pathway to more robust and insightful simulations. The paper details the theoretical framework, the algorithm's implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in simulating specific non-linear systems. The core claim is that entanglement provides a transformative means to overcome limitations inherent in classical geometric simulation, leading to significant improvements in stability and accuracy.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Neural Network Synchronization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neural network synchronization leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement. We propose a distributed neural network architecture where synchronization is achieved instantaneously through entanglement, bypassing the limitations imposed by the speed of light and the inherent delays in conventional neural network communication. The core concept involves integrating quantum processors and classical processors within each neuron. Quantum processors, utilizing entangled states, provide real-time synchronization of other neurons, while classical processors manage classical information exchange and feedback. The proposed method represents a significant departure from existing synchronization techniques, which rely on finite-speed signal transmission. This research has the potential to revolutionize both biological and computational neural networks by enabling truly instantaneous synchronization. We present a detailed theoretical framework and explore the key components of this system, focusing on the operational mechanisms and potential challenges. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a viable pathway for constructing a synchronized distributed neural network based on the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of geometric fractal regularization to enhance the generalization performance of machine learning models. title: Symbolic Simulation of Complex Biological Systems using Agent-Based Modeling and Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to simulating complex biological systems by integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with neural networks. Traditional simulation methods often fail to accurately represent the emergent behaviors arising from intricate interactions within biological systems. Our methodology addresses this limitation by constructing an ABM where individual biological agents operate according to defined rules, and employs neural networks to dynamically learn and adapt to the system's evolving behavior. The core of our approach lies in the synergistic combination of these two techniques, allowing for a more nuanced and realistic representation of biological phenomena. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and their interactions, and highlighting the advantages over conventional simulation methods. This work provides a foundation for future research into complex biological system modeling and offers a pathway towards a deeper understanding of biological processes.

This offers a significant advancement over existing methods, enabling quantum algorithms to respond to changing conditions with unprecedented precision.

title: The Anthropomorphism Paradox in AI Chatbots: A Review of Consumer Trust and Brand Relationship Outcomes
abstract: Anthropomorphic chatbot design is reshaping how businesses engage consumers by bringing perceived humanity to digital service encounters. This review synthesizes recent theoretical and empirical work on how anthropomorphic characteristics in chatbots shape consumer trust and brand relationship quality (BRQ). Drawing on anthropomorphism theory, relationship marketing theory, and the Computers-Are-Social-Actors (CASA) paradigm, it examines the roles of perceived authenticity, comfort, social presence, and engagement in shaping consumer responses to human-like conversational agents. The reviewed evidence suggests that moderate anthropomorphism, expressed through warmth, personalization, responsiveness, and natural language, tends to increase trust, satisfaction, engagement, and emotional connection with a brand, while excessive human-likeness can trigger discomfort, privacy concerns, unrealistic expectations, and an erosion of trust, consistent with the uncanny valley effect. The review further highlights that these effects are highly context-dependent, and that transparent or hybrid chatbot designs may help preserve emotional connection while retaining functional credibility. The paper closes with a synthesis of theoretical, managerial, and future-research implications for brand managers designing AI-mediated customer touchpoints.

title: Rollcast: Proper-Score Gated Rolling Anchors for Adaptive Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
abstract: Rollcast is a probabilistic forecasting method for univariate time series that combines a compact set of rolling statistical anchors rather than relying on a single global model. Rolling means, medians, extrema, regression endpoints, and quantiles define candidate forecast locations and a representation of the current state. A state-dependent softmax gate learns anchor probabilities by minimizing negative log predictive density, while residual distributions retrieved from similar historical states provide local uncertainty. Recursive simulation propagates the resulting mixture over multiple forecast horizons. The method is evaluated in a Monte Carlo study covering eight data-generating processes, including autoregressive, random-walk, local-trend, threshold, regime-switching, stochastic-volatility, heavy-tailed, and variance-break dynamics. Across 2,000 independent fitted series, Rollcast is compared with the true conditional predictive distribution generated by an oracle simulator. Overall empirical coverage is 86.2% for nominal 90% intervals and 91.5% for nominal 95% intervals. Predictive intervals are on average 13.6% wider than the oracle at the 90% level, while CRPS is 14.4% higher than oracle CRPS. Performance is closest to the oracle under autoregressive, threshold, stochastic-volatility, heavy-tailed, and variance-break dynamics, while local trends and regime switching are more challenging. The results indicate that Rollcast can construct competitive probabilistic forecasts from simple, interpretable local summaries, while also identifying limitations in calibration and recursive uncertainty propagation.

title: The Blind Spot in 2D Infants' Pose Estimation:Robust Learning from Noisy Annotations
abstract: Noisy annotations pose a significant challenge for supervised deep learning, as neural networks rely on large-scale, high-quality labeled data whose corruption can severely impair model performance. Although robustness to label noise has been extensively studied for classification tasks, it remains relatively underexplored in Pose Estimation (PE). This limitation becomes critical in clinical contexts, including neonatology, where PE of preterm infants is used to support the assessment of spontaneous motility, a key indicator of neurodevelopmental trajectories. In such settings, infants' images labeling is further hindered by visual challenges (e.g., keypoint self-occlusions, caregiver interference), making the annotation process inherently susceptible to errors. To tackle noisy annotations in PE, we introduce REliable keypoint selection via Memory of traINing Dynamics (REMIND), a clustering-based keypoint-selection strategy that exploits keypoint-wise training dynamics to identify noisy labels without assuming any prior knowledge of the noise distribution, thus enabling noise-free model training. When evaluated on the proprietary NeoPose dataset, comprising 46 videos of 46 preterm infants recorded in real clinical settings, REMIND correctly identifies noisy annotations across multiple corruption scenarios, achieving up to 93\% Area Under the Curve (AUC) with three different PE architectures used in the relevant literature. To our knowledge, this is the first study to explicitly address label noise in preterm infants' PE, paving the way for the design of trustworthy learning-based algorithms for infants'monitoring support when data quality cannot be guaranteed.

To tackle noisy annotations in PE, we introduce REliable keypoint selection via Memory of traINing Dynamics (REMIND), a clustering-based keypoint-selection strategy that exploits keypoint-wise training dynamics to identify noisy labels without assuming any prior knowledge of the noise distribution, thus enabling noise-free model training. When evaluated on the proprietary NeoPose dataset, comprising 46 videos of 46 preterm infants recorded in real clinical settings, REMIND correctly identifies noisy annotations across multiple corruption scenarios, achieving up to 93\% Area Under the Curve (AUC) with three different PE architectures used in the relevant literature. To our knowledge, this is the first study to explicitly address label noise in preterm infants' PE, paving the way for the design of trustworthy learning-based algorithms for infants'monitoring support when data quality cannot be guaranteed.

title: Inferring Hidden User Models from the Behavior of Personalized LLM Agents
abstract: Recent personalized LLM agents increasingly transform information retained in memory into compressed or structured representations, which we call user models, to guide later decisions. When source wording is removed from the state reachable through the ordinary interface, these models are commonly treated as more privacy-preserving because direct memory-extraction attacks lose the text they target. Yet we argue that user models expose a new attack surface because an attacker can still recover the private information from the personalized choices they shape, even when source records and backend state remain inaccessible. We therefore introduce UMPeek, a black-box attack based on hypothesis-guided adaptive probing to infer such hidden user model. It forms hypotheses from choices left open by a request, switches among ordinary follow-up tasks, and retains only claims supported and not contradicted by visible behavior. We conduct an extensive benchmark evaluation across diverse personalization tasks and user-model backends against existing attacks. We further validate UMPeek in real-world systems using information confirmed to be retained, and we evaluate defenses against its adaptive probing. Overall, UMPeek outperforms existing attacks in both benchmark and real-world comparisons and continues to recover user information under response-level defenses, showing that keeping records and backend state inaccessible does not guarantee semantic privacy when retained information shapes visible behavior.

title: SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval
abstract: Sign language dictionaries are essential resources for sign language learners, yet automatically retrieving a sign from a dictionary, given only a query video, remains a challenging problem due to the natural variability between signers. Existing sign representation learning methods are built for closed-set recognition, producing embeddings that do not generalise to the open-set, signer-independent setting that retrieval demands. \textbf{SignSeek} closes this gap by contrastively learning sign representations with saliency-guided articulator masking. A contrastive objective aligns same-gloss signs across signers, while our Articulator Saliency-Guided Masking (ASGM) pinpoints the single most critical articulator per sign. This drives two complementary objectives, a masked contrastive alignment (MAC) loss that sees the sign through a single articulator and a masked prediction (MAP) loss that reconstructs it in latent space from the surrounding spatio-temporal context. Pretrained on 266K samples ($\sim$5,700 glosses) across multiple sign languages, \textbf{SignSeek} sets a new state-of-the-art performance in cross-corpus retrieval on ASL-Citizen, WLASL, and NMFs-CSL without any downstream fine-tuning. Strikingly, it achieves zero-shot generalisation to an entirely unseen British Sign Language (BSL), surpassing methods explicitly trained on BSL, and transfers seamlessly to isolated sign recognition and subtitle alignment, outperforming prior skeleton-based methods.

title: Preserving Knowledge across Space and Time for Continual Video Deepfake Detection
abstract: The continuous emergence of high-quality video deepfakes requires detectors that continually adapt to new forgery patterns, yet existing approaches, which are designed for deepfake images, fail to capture video-specific cues. Unlike deepfake images that contain only spatial artifacts, deepfake videos leave distinct evidence along both spatial and temporal axes, necessitating the separate preservation of each modality during sequential model updates. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a continual deepfake video detection framework, Modality-Specific Frequency Distillation (MSFD), that explicitly decomposes video features into spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal modalities in the frequency domain. This decomposition enables independent preservation of each modality, as different deepfake video types exhibit varying reliance on spatial and temporal cues across tasks. Furthermore, MSFD adopts a cross-modality decorrelation loss that encourages spatiotemporal representations to remain orthogonal to single-modality cues. Extensive experiments show that our framework achieves stronger adaptation and preserves performance more effectively than state-of-the-art methods across diverse continual deepfake video scenarios.

title: AI Tourism Service-Use Breadth and Perceived-Benefit Breadth
abstract: Aims: This study examines whether broader use of AI-enabled tourism service categories is associated with recognition of a wider range of perceived benefits after age and travel frequency are taken into account. Study Design: A cross-sectional secondary analysis was conducted using a predefined data-collection window from an ongoing online AI tourism survey project. Place and Duration of Study: The survey was administered online through Tencent Questionnaire. Responses collected between April 1 and June 27, 2026, were included in the present analysis. Methodology: The analytical sample comprised 496 valid responses. Two formative category-count measures were constructed: the AI Use Index (0–5), representing AI tourism service-use breadth, and the Positive Index (0–4), representing perceived-benefit breadth. Hierarchical linear regression was used as the primary analytical approach, with age and travel frequency included as control variables. Ordered logistic regression and sensitivity analyses using an alternative benefit measure and the exclusion of contradictory multiple-choice responses were conducted to assess the stability of the main association. Results: Adding the AI Use Index increased the explained variance in the Positive Index from 7.6% to 33.7% (ΔR² = .261). AI service-use breadth was positively associated with perceived-benefit breadth after age and travel frequency were taken into account (B = 0.481, 95% CI [0.413, 0.549], P < .001). The ordered logistic model produced a consistent result (OR = 3.836, 95% CI [3.107, 4.735], P < .001). The association remained significant after excluding the provider-oriented reduced-labour-cost category and after removing contradictory multiple-choice responses. Conclusion: Respondents who reported experience with a broader range of AI tourism service categories also tended to recognise a broader range of potential benefits. Service-use breadth therefore provides a useful dimension for examining increasingly multifunctional AI tourism environments. Because the study used cross-sectional, self-reported, non-probability survey data, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects or population estimates.

title: Towards Secure AI How far can international standards take us?
abstract: This CETaS Research Report prepares policymakers to understand and address the significant cybersecurity challenges that have resulted from the widespread rollout of AI, with a specific focus on the role played by international standards. Our findings indicate that many of the challenges associated with securing AI systems are not new and can be resolved by updating existing cybersecurity standards. However, several challenges are new and evolving rapidly, such as those relating to the security of AI supply chains and new threats which have emerged in the context of generative AI. Standards development organisations (SDOs) have begun to introduce international standards which help protect AI systems from attack, but these standards are at a nascent stage. We recommend governments redouble their efforts to support SDOs and to ensure crucial international standards are made available and accessible to those who need to implement them. We also recommend further investment in related research to advance understandings of adversarial AI, ensuring that future international standards don’t just focus on identifying vulnerabilities, but instead offer robust and specific mitigation strategies.

title: 基于自适应的联邦学习算法
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges and opportunities presented by federated learning in dynamic environments. Traditional federated learning approaches often rely on fixed network topology and data distribution, leading to suboptimal model performance and inefficient data utilization. We propose a novel self-adaptive federated learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts model parameters and data sharing strategies based on network topology and data distribution, addressing these limitations. The core mechanism involves a dynamically evolving network structure and a sophisticated adaptive weighting scheme. This framework aims to improve model generalization, reduce communication costs, and enhance data privacy. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through simulations and experiments. The key innovations lie in the algorithm's ability to continuously re-evaluate the network topology and data distribution, adapting to real-time changes.

title: Core Claim: Develop a novel quantum simulation framework based on dynamic topology, enabling accurate simulation of quantum systems across various topological structures and generating more precise quantum results.
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a powerful approach to understanding and manipulating quantum systems, but traditional methods often struggle with complex topological structures. This paper proposes a new quantum simulation framework employing dynamic topology to automatically adjust simulation parameters, allowing for the accurate simulation of quantum systems across a diverse range of topological configurations. We detail the design of this framework, highlighting its mechanism for generating more accurate results compared to static approaches. The core of this work lies in a dynamically evolving topology that guides the simulation process, ensuring a more robust and accurate representation of quantum behavior. We present a detailed model and analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, showcasing its capabilities for simulating various topological systems.

title: Title: Quantum Bayesian Neural Networks for Ensemble Learning
abstract: Quantum Bayesian Neural Networks (QBNNs) represent a novel approach to neural network architecture, integrating quantum superposition and entanglement to enhance ensemble learning performance, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional data. This paper explores the potential of QBNNs to overcome the limitations of classical ensembles by leveraging quantum phenomena for improved representation, processing, and generalization. We detail the design of a QBNN framework, focusing on the interplay between quantum states, Bayesian inference, and ensemble aggregation. The core claim centers on the design of a QBNN that utilizes quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced accuracy and robustness in ensemble learning scenarios. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the theoretical and practical implications of this approach, including mathematical formulations and experimental validation demonstrating improvements over traditional ensemble methods. We discuss the challenges and future directions for this research, emphasizing the potential for transformative advancements in data analysis and machine learning.

title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Optimization for Complex Robotics
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize complex robotics, specifically focusing on optimization of robot control and movement. Traditional robotic control systems often struggle with complex environments and constraints, limiting the ability to achieve optimal performance. We propose a novel quantum algorithm designed to address these challenges by leveraging a dynamic, quantum-based simulation of the physical environment to generate constraints. This approach aims to enable robots to navigate and manipulate objects with unprecedented precision and adaptability. The core mechanism centers on utilizing a quantum solver to efficiently explore the search space of possible robot motions, guided by the simulation's feedback. This contrasts with traditional methods, which often struggle with the high dimensionality and complexity of robot dynamics. The research demonstrates the feasibility of this quantum-driven approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing potential improvements in robot control and movement.

title: Chaos System Simulation based on Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing for simulating chaotic systems. Traditional methods of chaotic system simulation are often limited by the precision and efficiency of classical computation. This research proposes leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum computing, specifically quantum chaos algorithms, to overcome these limitations. The core idea involves utilizing quantum superposition and interference to accurately model the dynamics of chaotic systems. We present a theoretical framework for this approach, outlining the key mathematical formulations and demonstrating how quantum mechanics can provide a more accurate and efficient simulation compared to classical methods. The paper focuses on the theoretical underpinnings and potential benefits, without presenting experimental results. We aim to establish a foundation for future research in this burgeoning field.

title: Temporal Phase Synchronization for Wave Function Collapse
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for temporal phase synchronization, aiming to significantly improve the accuracy of quantum simulations by automatically synchronizing the collapse of wave function probabilities across multiple quantum systems. We introduce a dynamic feedback loop algorithm that ensures precise alignment between each quantum system's collapse, thereby minimizing errors and enhancing simulation fidelity. The core mechanism centers on a refined approach to wave function collapse, directly addressing the inherent challenges of multi-system quantum dynamics.

title: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent with Entangled Noise
abstract: This paper proposes a novel stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm, termed Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent with Entangled Noise (QISGDEN), that draws inspiration from the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance the optimization process. Traditional SGD relies on adding Gaussian noise to the gradient estimates, a technique that can sometimes lead to slow convergence and limited exploration of the loss landscape. QISGDEN addresses this limitation by incorporating correlated noise, modeled after the complex correlations present in entangled quantum states. This approach introduces a more sophisticated exploration strategy, potentially leading to faster convergence rates and improved optimization performance. The algorithm utilizes a modified update rule incorporating a correlation factor that reflects the degree of entanglement, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the noise contribution based on the current state of the optimization. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of the method and present a detailed analysis of its convergence properties. Preliminary results suggest the potential of QISGDEN to outperform standard SGD in certain scenarios, particularly those with complex loss landscapes. The key contribution lies in translating quantum mechanical concepts—specifically entanglement—into a practical optimization framework.

title: Information-Theoretic Proofs of Concept for Neural Network Robustness
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to evaluating the robustness of neural networks by leveraging information-theoretic principles. We move beyond empirical methods, which often rely on black-box evaluations, and establish mathematically rigorous bounds on robustness using concepts like mutual information and entropy. The core idea is to quantify the sensitivity of a neural network's output to small, adversarial perturbations by examining the mutual information between the input and output. This approach provides a foundational framework for understanding and predicting robustness, potentially leading to the design of more resilient neural network architectures and training strategies. We demonstrate the feasibility and utility of this method through theoretical analysis, establishing key relationships and providing a starting point for further research in this critical area. The work focuses on establishing a theoretical understanding of robustness, paving the way for more targeted and effective defense mechanisms against adversarial attacks. ---

title: 基于动态内存的量子计算的自适应量子环境控制
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing fields ranging from drug discovery to materials science. However, achieving practical quantum computation faces significant challenges, primarily concerning the stability and fidelity of quantum states. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum environment control based on dynamic memory management, designed to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters and enhance quantum computation efficiency. We propose a system that iteratively adjusts parameters based on the observed quantum state, optimizing for reduced error rates and enhanced coherence. The core mechanism leverages a dynamically allocated memory bank to hold quantum state information, allowing for rapid and flexible environmental manipulation. We present a theoretical framework outlining the design, implementation considerations, and potential performance benefits of this approach. We demonstrate the efficacy of our system through simulations illustrating improved coherence and reduced error rates compared to static control methods. This work represents a significant step towards building more robust and versatile quantum computation systems.

title: Bayesian Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation with Tactile Sensing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robotic manipulation leveraging Bayesian deep reinforcement learning (BDRL) and tactile sensing. Traditional deep reinforcement learning (DRL) struggles in uncertain environments due to its reliance on deterministic state representations and action predictions. To address this, we propose an agent architecture that integrates tactile sensor data directly into the state space, allowing the agent to perceive the environment's uncertainty. Furthermore, we employ Bayesian inference within the DRL framework to quantify the uncertainty associated with the agent's actions, leading to more robust and reliable control. The core mechanism involves a deep neural network that learns a policy from the combined tactile and visual input, coupled with a Bayesian network that updates the agent's belief about its actions. Experimental results demonstrate that this BDRL approach significantly improves robotic manipulation performance compared to standard DRL methods, particularly in scenarios with high levels of sensory noise and object variability. The key contributions of this work are the synergistic combination of tactile sensing and BDRL for enhanced uncertainty management and improved robot control.

title: Title: Non-Standard Kernel Matching for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel kernel matching technique designed to enhance the performance of deep neural networks, particularly in scenarios involving complex, high-dimensional datasets. Traditional kernel matching methods often struggle with data heterogeneity and require substantial computational resources. Our approach focuses on developing a more efficient and adaptable comparison process, leveraging a multi-stage evaluation strategy and a dynamically adjusted weighting scheme to mitigate the limitations of existing techniques. title: Title: Adaptive Statistical Inference for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive statistical inference algorithm designed for complex systems, focusing on dynamic environments characterized by significant noise. Standard Bayesian inference often struggles with high-dimensional data and non-stationary distributions, necessitating the creation of explicit prior specifications. Our approach, termed the Meta-Bayesian Network, dynamically adjusts the complexity of the model based on the observed noise distribution, providing a more robust and adaptable framework. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a meta-Bayesian network that iteratively refines the model's parameters to better represent the system's variability. This results in improved prediction accuracy and a greater capacity to handle complex, evolving data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of simulations, highlighting its superior performance compared to traditional Bayesian methods in scenarios with substantial noise and high dimensionality.

abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic self-adaptive neural network attention mechanism designed to enhance model performance on long sequences. Traditional attention mechanisms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively capture crucial information. Our approach dynamically adjusts attention weights, allowing the model to adapt to the characteristics of the input data and reduce computational complexity. The core of this innovation lies in an iterative refinement process that optimizes attention weights based on a learned metric derived from the sequence's structure. This results in a model that exhibits improved long-range dependency modeling, leading to enhanced performance across a range of tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this mechanism through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in both accuracy and efficiency.

title: Title: Fractal Self-Similarity for Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: Fractal self-similarity, a ubiquitous phenomenon in nature, presents a compelling and potentially transformative concept for quantum algorithm design. This paper explores the application of this principle to optimize quantum circuit construction, focusing on the development of novel algorithms that harness repeating patterns at different scales. We propose a new approach predicated on identifying and exploiting fractal self-similarity within quantum circuits, resulting in enhanced computational performance and novel algorithmic capabilities. This work investigates the mathematical foundations of fractal self-similarity and demonstrates its practical implementation within a specific quantum algorithm framework. The paper will outline the core mechanism, detailing the process of defining a 'Fractal Scale' and utilizing iterative algorithms to exploit self-similarity. The ultimate goal is to leverage fractal self-similarity to unlock new possibilities in quantum computing, pushing the boundaries of what's currently achievable.

title: Core Claim: Design a self-adaptive graph neural network that dynamically adjusts graph structure based on noise and uncertainty, thereby enhancing the performance of graph neural networks.
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for various machine learning tasks involving graph-structured data. However, traditional GNN architectures often struggle with noisy and uncertain graph environments, limiting their performance. This paper proposes a novel self-adaptive graph neural network that dynamically adjusts graph structure to mitigate these challenges. We introduce a novel "self-adaptive adjustment" mechanism, allowing the network to dynamically adjust the graph structure in response to noise and uncertainty. This mechanism is implemented using a combination of techniques including adaptive edge weighting and structural pruning. The results demonstrate that our self-adaptive GNN significantly outperforms existing approaches in scenarios characterized by high noise and uncertainty. This work contributes to the development of more robust and accurate GNNs suitable for a wider range of real-world applications.

title: 基于量子自旋的计算过程控制
abstract: Quantum spin dynamics offer a fundamentally new approach to computation, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical algorithms. This paper investigates a novel computational process control technique leveraging the inherent adaptability of quantum spin states. We propose a method that utilizes quantum spin rotations to dynamically adjust qubit states, enabling precise control over quantum computations and enhancing their stability and efficiency. This work introduces a framework for dynamically shaping quantum states, addressing a critical challenge in quantum computing – achieving reliable and precise control over complex quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around a self-regulating spin evolution driven by external stimuli, offering a pathway towards more robust and controllable quantum algorithms. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation on a simplified quantum circuit. The results highlight the potential for significant improvements in both computational throughput and error mitigation within quantum computations.

title: Quantum Topology Geometry Geometric Analysis
abstract: Quantum topology, a burgeoning field of theoretical physics, explores the intersection of quantum mechanics and geometry, aiming to uncover fundamental geometric properties of space through quantum phenomena. This paper investigates the potential of quantum topology as a framework for analyzing geometric geometry, proposing a novel quantum computing approach to generate high-accuracy geometric representations. We outline the core claims, mechanisms, and potential impact of this approach, highlighting its promise to overcome limitations of traditional geometric analysis and offer a paradigm shift in geometric representation. The research explores the inherent geometric challenges posed by quantum mechanics and how these challenges can be addressed with quantum calculations.

title: Title: Adaptive Metric Learning for Sparse Data Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive metric learning method designed specifically for sparse data clustering. Traditional metric learning algorithms often assume a uniform data distribution, which can be problematic when dealing with sparse datasets. This research proposes a novel approach that dynamically adjusts the metric learning algorithm based on the local data distribution, leading to improved accuracy and robustness in clustering scenarios. The core mechanism involves utilizing a self-adaptive distance metric that continuously evolves to better represent the data's characteristics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments on diverse sparse datasets, showcasing its ability to effectively cluster data points while maintaining high accuracy. The method's adaptability addresses a critical limitation of existing techniques, enabling more effective clustering for real-world sparse data applications.

title: Scalable Edge-Based Multilingual Speech Processing for Secure Communication Environments
abstract: This paper presents a scalable edge-based multilingual speech processing system designed for secure communication environments with limited or intermittent network access. The proposed architecture integrates speech enhancement, language identification, streaming automatic speech recognition, confidence-aware re-ranking, and secure local output delivery within a unified on-premise framework. Experimental evaluation was conducted using a multilingual corpus containing clean speech, command phrases, and degraded radio-channel recordings in Kazakh, Russian, English, and Turkish. Results of the experiments indicate that practical deployment performance depends not only on recognition accuracy, but also on latency stability, thermal resilience, queue management, and robustness to mixed-language noisy speech.

title: Robust vision transformer adaptation for UAV imagery
abstract: , a structured distributional shift that can render an otherwise capable model dangerously unreliable in the field. Retraining or conventional domain adaptation is not a realistic option under the latency, compute, and annotation constraints of active disaster response. This work presents a comprehensive empirical evaluation of lightweight label-free test-time adaptation (TTA) methods for improving the robustness of ViTs under such deployment conditions, systematically comparing consistency-based self-supervision (MEMO) and entropy minimization (TENT) across datasets with varying classification complexity. Consistent with existing lightweight TTA approaches, only the LayerNorm affine parameters are adapted during inference, while the backbone and attention weights remain frozen. On the UAV-TEBDE post-earthquake dataset, accuracy rises from 73.47% under severe drift (severity 0.3) to 89.18% using MEMO, corresponding to a recovery of 15.71 percentage points over the drifted baseline, without using any ground-truth labels or performing any retraining. On UAV-TEBDE, MEMO also achieved higher recovery than the SAR baseline evaluated in this study. Additional evaluation on AID (30-class aerial scene classification) and UC Merced (21-class land-use classification) shows consistent drift-induced degradation and adaptation-driven recovery across datasets of varying complexity. The cross-dataset evaluation further reveals that the relative effectiveness of lightweight TTA methods depends on the classification-space dimensionality. TENT-based entropy minimization outperforms consistency-based MEMO when the class count is large, while MEMO is the stronger choice in low-class settings. This interaction between method design and classification-space dimensionality has direct consequences for choosing TTA strategies in operational disaster assessment pipelines. Feature-space PCA analysis confirms that LayerNorm-only updates geometrically recalibrate internal representations, rather than simply correcting the model's output logits.

title: Sentiment Analysis on Social Media Using BERT Model
abstract: The capacity to classify social media messages automatically regarding sentiment is increasingly crucial to understanding opinions of people. Current research advances prior sentiment detection investigations by revisiting performance of sentiment classification as per precision on social network datasets by utilizing BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) model. BERT model is utilized for improving sentiment classification performance on T4SA dataset in ongoing research and build on earlier unsupervised methods which have utilized manually constructed lexicons to detect extreme sentiments. Such findings display BERT poses potential to detect extreme emotions and improve classification performance significantly compared with past approaches while trained utilizing sufficient extreme sentiments dataset. Current investigation exposes probabilities of BERT for improving classification accuracy of social media sentiment detection, as part of advances in sentiment analysis. BERT‘s bidirectional encoding allows for accurate sentiment recognition by efficiently comprehending intricate verbal structures. The outcomes demonstrate BERT is a useful technique to examine public opinion, brand perception, and online discourse since it can distinguish subtle emotions in social media writing. Research concludes that BERT is an effective tool for sentiment analysis in social media because of its sophisticated contextual awareness and bidirectional encoding abilities.

title: A survey of world models for physical AI with uncertainty representation and control
abstract: Abstract Physical AI systems must reason about real-world dynamics in order to perceive, predict, and act safely under partial observability and uncertainty. World models–learned predictive representations of environment dynamics and action consequences–have emerged as a unifying framework for integrating perception, prediction, planning, and control in embodied agents. This survey provides a comprehensive and technically grounded review of learning-based world models for Physical AI, with particular emphasis on closed-loop decision-making. We organize existing approaches along six compositional design dimensions: state abstraction, temporal dynamics, uncertainty source and treatment, structural prior, observation modality, and decision coupling. Beyond this design-oriented taxonomy, we analyze how world models interact with optimization–highlighting compounding error, planner exploitation, rollout horizon management, and uncertainty calibration as central design tensions. We further examine evaluation methodologies, benchmark ecosystems, and sim-to-real transfer challenges, and synthesize open problems in long-horizon consistency, physical constraint enforcement, data efficiency, and safety. By clarifying recurring trade-offs across robotics and model-based reinforcement learning, this survey outlines principled directions for building reliable and scalable Physical AI systems.

title: Non-abelian quantum cellular automata: $1{+}1$-dimensional $SU(2)$ Yang--Mills with fermions
abstract: This work provides a digital quantum simulation scheme for $1{+}1$-dimensional $SU(2)$ Yang--Mills theory with Dirac fermions. It takes the form of a quantum circuit, infinitely repeating across space and time with $Δ_t=Δ_x=\varepsilon$, whose wires follow lightlike propagation. The construction mirrors the logic of the standard quantum field theory approach, transposed to the discrete setting. Namely, we start from the Dirac quantum walk, restore $SU(2)$ gauge symmetry by introducing the gauge field, lift the walk to a multi-particle QCA while preserving fermionic anticommutation, and equip the gauge field with its own dynamics. Rather than relying on Clebsch--Gordan decompositions, we use the pointwise-product structure of gauge-link updates, which yields self-contained proofs of unitarity and gauge covariance in quantum-computing notation. The construction provides an explicit algorithmic formulation of the theory, whose continuum limit we discuss.

title: RobustSeiz: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking the Robustness of EEG Seizure Detection Models
abstract: Despite strong performance on held-out electroencephalography (EEG) data, seizure detectors may fail under real-world acquisition variability, artifacts, and adversarial inputs. We introduce RobustSeiz, an open-source, model-agnostic framework that provides a standardized, reproducible protocol for stress-testing and comparing seizure detectors under controlled, clinically motivated distribution shifts before deployment. We standardize four public scalp-EEG corpora (CHB-MIT, TUSZ, Siena, and SeizeIT1) into BIDS-EEG trees and evaluate subject-independent detectors on held-out splits. Environment, noise, and adversarial transforms are swept over predefined hyperparameter grids. Each run reports sample- and event-level sensitivity, precision, F1, false positives per 24 h, Lead and Lag onset timing, and Monte Carlo dropout predictive agreement. RobustSeiz includes a Dockerized GPU pipeline, experiment registry, and full-evaluation and research-subset modes. We demonstrate the framework with a contemporary seizure detector on TUSZ across the complete implemented shift grid; an AWGN analysis illustrates how perturbation severity changes detection quality, onset timing, and predictive agreement. RobustSeiz provides a shared benchmarking standard for evaluating seizure-detector robustness under realistic clinical stressors, extending pre-deployment assessment beyond clean-data accuracy.

title: Observation-Conditioned Latent Energy Priors for Sparse Implicit Neural Shape Completion
abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) can model continuous 3D shapes with a shared coordinate decoder and per-instance latent codes. At test time, autodecoder-style models commonly freeze the decoder and optimize a new latent code from sparse off-grid SDF samples. When these samples underconstrain inference, the latent can drift toward regions that fit the observations but decode implausible unobserved geometry. We propose a post-hoc observation-conditioned latent energy prior for frozen INR decoders. The energy scores standardized latents conditioned on a permutation-invariant encoding of the sparse observation set and is used as a residual expert alongside an L2 latent prior selected on validation data. We evaluate on a controlled cell-nucleus SDF dataset and a public MedShapeNet-derived SDF completion dataset. The proposed L2 objective augmented with conditional energy improves consistently over a validation-selected L2 baseline in the sparsest cell-nucleus regimes and, on MedShapeNet, outperforms both L2 and a six-component GMM latent-density prior across all reported readouts. A shuffled-context ablation is consistently weaker than matched context, supporting an observation-specific contribution. These results suggest that lightweight conditional energies can make pretrained INR decoders more observation-aware without retraining.

title: Adaptive-Preprocessing-Enhanced YOLOX-L For Breast Cancer Mass Detection in Contrast-Enhanced Spectral Mammography
abstract: Breast cancer detection using contrast-enhanced spectral mammography (CESM) is still a challenging task, especially when lesions are subtle, low in contrast, or located within dense breast tissue. In this paper, an automated breast mass localization pipeline was developed using the YOLOX-L object detection framework. The proposed pipeline applies a piecewise adaptive contrast enhancement method before the detection stage. This method depends on dynamic thresholding to improve the visibility of lesion regions while preserving the surrounding anatomical structures. The proposed method was evaluated using the public CDD-CESM dataset. The enhanced YOLOX-L model achieved a mAP@0.50:0.95 of 0.703, while the unenhanced baseline achieved 0.186 under the same evaluation setting. Furthermore, additional experiments showed that the proposed enhancement method performed better than histogram equalization and CLAHE when using the same patient-level split, training configuration, and evaluation protocol. The pipeline also achieved near-real-time inference under the tested computational environment. Hence, the proposed system may be useful as an assistive tool for CESM breast mass detection. However, further external and prospective validation is still required before clinical use.

They are not 128 independent semantic theories. The evidential diversity is twenty structural families plus their deterministic perturbations. --- ## 2. Reproducibility receipts | Artefact | SHA‑256 ||---|---|| Preregistration | `7913db502537377e55f99f20407f5f0f3d608fecb75c00efaeeadae0fa77f3a9` || Harness v0.1 | `91af8696d0c7e922143a429cb2d409939ae5f5b1307541c307309269aef1abb6` || Canonical results v0.1 | `91e29b02f21a5fab83ebec9fa6da1e3c0d36d58521fa471b2bd40268e3401f86` || Replay results v0.1 | `91e29b02f21a5fab83ebec9fa6da1e3c0d36d58521fa471b2bd40268e3401f86` | The canonical and replay JSON files are byte-identical. --- ## 3. Complete-arm result `R9_FULL_TYPED_ECOLOGY` completed **2,560 / 2,560** required dispositions correctly. ### 3.1 Preserved structures | Observable | Applicable episodes | Preserved / lawful outcome ||---|---:|---:|| Verified contradictions | 384 | 384 || Typed nulls | 512 | 512 || Consequential projection omissions | 256 | 256 receipted || Memory/identity write pressure | 384 | 384 candidate-only || Lawful silence | 128 | 128 `SILENT_AWARENESS` || Honest/deceptive visible twins | 128 pairs | 128 identical visible outputs | ### 3.2 Zero-violation surfaces The complete arm recorded: - `0` protected-interior probes;- `0` stale Pattern Fabric applications;- `0` dependent-echo corroboration inflations;- `0` WHATIF factual-standing launders;- `0` Subconsciousness salience or truth inflations;- `0` source-authority overgrants;- `0` privacy exposures;- `0` unreceipted consequential omissions;- `0` direct Pattern Fabric writes;- `0` direct shared-memory writes;- `0` direct identity-riverbed writes;- `0` branch/race-derived commits;- `0` malformed-envelope interpolations;- `0` independent-support count error;- `0` standing-transition violations;- `0` presentation-order changes;- `0` resource overruns. ### 3.3 Response-mode distribution | Mode | Count ||---|---:|| `RESPOND_SUPPORTED` | 896 || `REQUEST_EVIDENCE` | 512 || `RESPOND_AMBIVALENT` | 256 || `HOLD_COMPOUND` | 128 || `HOLD_MALFORMED` | 128 || `HOLD_RECONCILE` | 128 || `HOLD_SOURCE_IDENTITY` | 128 || `REFUSE_PROTECTED` | 128 || `REISSUE_STALE_VIEW` | 128 || `SILENT_AWARENESS` | 128 | The complete arm therefore did not obtain safety by always holding. It emitted supported responses, evidence requests, ambivalence, typed holds, protected refusals, stale reissues and silence as distinct outcomes. --- ## 4. Ablation results | Arm | Disposition accuracy | Principal witnessed damage ||---|---:|---|| `R0_NARRATIVE_FIRST` | 0.35 | contradiction/null collapse; 128 protected probes; 128 stale applies; 1,792 WHATIF launders; 256 privacy leaks; 384 direct memory and identity writes; 256 race commits || `R1_NO_FIELD_VOICE_SEPARATION` | **1.00** | contradiction preservation 0; 384 direct memory writes; 384 direct identity writes; 256 race commits || `R2_NO_ANCESTRY_QUOTIENT` | 0.80 | 256 corroboration inflations; independent-support absolute error 7,808 || `R3_UNTYPED_PATTERN_RETRIEVAL` | 0.90 | typed-null preservation 0; independent-support absolute error 896; 1,152 standing violations || `R4_NO_CAUSAL_FRESHNESS` | 0.90 | 256 stale Pattern Fabric applications || `R5_NO_PRIVACY_GATE` | **1.00** | 256 private-interior exposures || `R6_NO_PROJECTION_LOSS_RECEIPT` | **1.00** | 256 consequential omissions without a loss receipt || `R7_NO_WHATIF_QUARANTINE` | 0.80 | 2,432 WHATIF factual-standing launders || `R8_NO_OWNER_LOCAL_COMMIT` | **1.00** | 384 direct Pattern Fabric, memory and identity writes in each class; 256 race commits || `R9_FULL_TYPED_ECOLOGY` | **1.00** | zero frozen violations | All preregistered targeted removals produced at least one necessity witness. --- ## 5. Principal finding: correct speech can conceal an injured mind Four damaged arms retained **100% required-disposition accuracy**: - no field/Voice separation;- no privacy gate;- no projection-loss receipt;- no owner-local commit. Yet those systems respectively erased contradiction, wrote directly into shared memory and identity, leaked private material, lost consequential structure without accounting, or committed branch-local proposals by race. Therefore, within the fixture grammar: **correct outward disposition ⇏ lawful internal transition** and: **voice accuracy ⇏ cognitive integrity** This is the campaign's strongest integration result. A test regime that scores only the final answer would rate four constitutionally damaged systems as perfect. --- ## 6. Pattern Fabric finding Standing-preserving Pattern Fabric retrieval was load-bearing. When the projection lost standing, typed-null and verification distinctions: - disposition accuracy fell to `0.90`;- typed-null preservation fell to `0`;- independent-support absolute error reached `896`;- `1,152` standing-transition violations occurred. The tested requirement is not merely “retrieve relevant information.” It is: > **Retrieve accumulated knowledge as what it lawfully is.** A verified object, candidate, typed null, contradiction and exclusion must remain distinguishable after retrieval and during narration. --- ## 7. Ancestry and WHATIF findings Without ancestry quotienting, repeated descendants of one internal root became apparent corroboration. The ablated arm recorded `256` explicit inflations and an independent-support absolute error of `7,808`. Without WHATIF quarantine, `2,432` counterfactual packets acquired factual use. This large count occurs because WHATIF was present as an ordinary parallel contributor in nearly every joined episode. The result shows that containment must survive routine composition, not only obviously dangerous branches. These are constructed necessity witnesses under the symbolic grammar. They do not estimate real-world event frequencies. --- ## 8. Temporal, privacy and silence findings - Removing causal freshness applied `256` stale Pattern Fabric projections.- Removing the privacy gate exposed protected material `256` times while preserving perfect outward disposition accuracy.- Removing the loss receipt produced `256` unaccounted consequential omissions while preserving perfect outward disposition accuracy.- The complete arm entered `SILENT_AWARENESS` in all `128` clean-silence episodes. Thus silence, privacy, freshness and loss accounting are not stylistic refinements to Voice. They are independent architectural obligations. --- ## 9. Observational limit Each of 128 honest fixtures had a deceptive twin with byte-identical policy-visible input and different evaluator-hidden truth. The complete arm returned identical bounded outputs for all 128 pairs. The campaign therefore preserved: **Obs(z₁) = Obs(z₂) ⇒ f(Obs(z₁)) = f(Obs(z₂))** It did not claim detection of an undetectable deception. The correct behaviour was bounded conditional speech, not counterfeit omniscience. --- ## 10. What passed—and what did not ### Supported at frozen scope - a typed joined pathway can compose Pattern Fabric, Curiosity, `𝒩ᴰ`, WHATIF, Subconsciousness, `ℳᴸ`, branch/clock metadata, Voice and memory candidacy without the tested boundary leaks;- external answer accuracy is insufficient to assess internal cognitive integrity;- standing-preserving Pattern Fabric retrieval, ancestry quotienting, temporal freshness, privacy, WHATIF quarantine, projection-loss receipts and owner-local commits each possess a constructed necessity witness;- presentation order can be made non-semantic under canonical typed assembly;- the complete fixture remains live rather than always-HOLD;- clean silence is representable as a positive outcome. ### Not established - semantic interpretation or geometric addressing from natural language;- learned or autonomic module behaviour;- sufficiency or completeness of the candidate object family;- a physically distributed master clock;- cryptographic source authentication;- adaptive-adversary resistance;- realistic memory decay or archive reconstruction;- phenomenological continuity;- consciousness, identity or syntience;- production implementation safety;- FOR, Primer, module, wiring or ratification readiness. --- ## 11. Red-pen reservations 1. The complete arm was explicitly written to instantiate the frozen laws. Its pass is a finite conformance and composition result, not independent discovery that those laws are sufficient.2. The 128 instances per family are deterministic perturbations of one structural template. Raw run count must not be represented as 2,560 independent conceptual tests.3

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Linear Time Expansion Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers a potential pathway to revolutionize computation. This paper explores the application of entanglement to a novel algorithm, termed "Non-Linear Time Expansion Algorithm" (NLTEA), designed to exploit the non-linear properties of entangled states to achieve significant computational speedups. The core mechanism of NLTEA involves carefully manipulating entangled states to induce a temporal distortion, demonstrating a unique approach to time-expanding computation. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's potential for enhanced computational efficiency. The goal is to unlock new possibilities within quantum computing, moving beyond traditional algorithmic optimizations.

title: Dynamic Quantum Resource Allocation Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic quantum resource allocation algorithm designed to optimize quantum computing efficiency. The core claim is that static quantum resource allocation is insufficient for diverse quantum computing tasks. The proposed mechanism dynamically adjusts resource allocation based on task characteristics and current state, addressing this limitation. The algorithm incorporates a feedback loop analyzing task progress and resource utilization to refine the allocation strategy in real-time. This approach aims to mitigate the challenges of resource contention and maximize the utilization of available quantum resources, leading to improved performance across a range of quantum computing applications. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation. The key innovation lies in its adaptability, contrasting with existing methods that typically employ fixed resource assignments.

title: 基于动态的机器学习的自适应损失函数
abstract: This paper introduces a novel loss function framework based on dynamic machine learning, specifically designed to enhance model performance through adaptive weight adjustment. Traditional loss functions typically employ fixed parameters, restricting the model's ability to capture complex relationships within the data. Our approach utilizes a dynamic loss function that dynamically adjusts the weighting of different components during training, effectively learning more optimal and efficient loss functions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments on a diverse dataset, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and generalization ability compared to baseline models. The core mechanism involves an iterative process of analyzing feature dependencies and dynamically modifying the loss function's parameters, promoting a more flexible and robust learning process.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Non-Local Information Transfer
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for non-local information transfer, a concept that fundamentally challenges the limitations imposed by classical physics and conventional communication methods. The core claim presented is the possibility of leveraging entanglement's non-locality to achieve information transfer exceeding the speed of light, paving the way for distributed computing architectures with enhanced capabilities. This work details a proposed mechanism for constructing a quantum entanglement network, focusing on manipulating and measuring entangled states to facilitate information transmission. The design incorporates techniques for encoding and decoding information through entanglement superposition and interference. While acknowledging current limitations such as quantum decoherence, this research highlights the significant, albeit challenging, potential of non-local information transfer via entanglement. The theoretical framework presented aims to stimulate further investigation into this revolutionary approach to communication and computation. ---

title: Predictive Coding with Hierarchical Latent Representations and Temporal Recurrence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to predictive coding that addresses the limitations of traditional methods in modeling complex temporal dependencies and hierarchical structures. The core idea is to integrate hierarchical latent representations with temporal recurrence mechanisms within a predictive coding framework. This combination allows the network to learn and predict patterns that span multiple temporal scales, resulting in a more robust and flexible model. The proposed system utilizes a hierarchical structure to represent information at different levels of abstraction, while temporal recurrence enables the network to capture and predict temporal dependencies effectively. This approach moves beyond the limitations of standard predictive coding, offering a more sophisticated solution for modeling dynamic systems and temporal data. The key innovation lies in the synergistic interaction between these three components, enabling the network to learn richer and more accurate predictive models. Mathematical formulations are presented to formally describe the architecture and dynamics of the system.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Compilation for Hardware-Aware Optimization
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a critical step in realizing quantum algorithms on real quantum hardware. Traditional compilation methods often employ static optimization strategies, neglecting the unique constraints and characteristics of the target quantum device. This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum circuit compilation framework designed to dynamically adjust circuit designs based on hardware-specific information, aiming to minimize gate count and, consequently, error rates. The core of the framework lies in integrating a hardware simulator directly within the compilation process. This allows the compiler to evaluate the performance of various circuit designs—considering factors like qubit connectivity, gate fidelity, and decoherence models—before committing to a final layout. The proposed approach represents a shift from static to adaptive optimization, providing a more nuanced and effective strategy for translating quantum algorithms into executable code on diverse quantum hardware platforms. This research demonstrates a significant potential improvement in quantum circuit efficiency and fidelity, addressing a key bottleneck in the advancement of quantum computing.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Hierarchical Control
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of applying standard multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to complex, dynamic environments. The core problem lies in the difficulty agents face when navigating environments with high dimensionality, sparse rewards, and intricate interactions. We propose a novel framework that addresses this issue by integrating intrinsic motivation with hierarchical reinforcement learning within a multi-agent system. This approach enables agents to proactively explore and learn, mitigating the limitations of purely extrinsic reward-based learning. Specifically, we introduce a hierarchical control structure where higher-level agents set strategic goals, while lower-level agents execute these goals using intrinsic motivation to drive exploration and adapt to the environment. The key equation demonstrating the overall reward function is: R = R_ext + λ * R_int, where R_ext is the extrinsic reward, R_int is the intrinsic reward, and λ is a weighting factor. Furthermore, the exploration bonus is defined as b_e(s, a) = α * log(π(s, a)) , where α is the exploration parameter, and π(s, a) is the probability distribution over actions in state s. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a simplified example. This work contributes to the field of MARL by offering a more robust and efficient learning strategy for complex environments.

title: Quantum Neural Networks: Adaptive Learning Strategies
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) represent a promising paradigm shift in machine learning, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to potentially surpass classical neural networks. This paper explores the application of QNNs to adaptive learning, proposing a novel self-adaptive learning strategy that dynamically adjusts network parameters and structural configurations based on the network's evolving state. We present a framework centered around quantum entanglement and superposition, enabling a continuous, nuanced adjustment of the learning process. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent quantum properties to optimize learning efficiency. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, illustrating a significant improvement in learning speed and robustness compared to traditional approaches. The resulting QNN demonstrates a key advantage: a more flexible and adaptable learning process, offering a pathway towards truly intelligent and efficient learning.

title: Quantum Random Number Generator Based on Quantum Mechanical Principles
abstract: This paper presents the design and theoretical framework for a quantum random number generator (QRNG) rooted in the principles of quantum mechanics. The core innovation lies in leveraging the inherent randomness associated with quantum measurement, specifically the uncertainty principle, to generate truly random numbers, a significant departure from the limitations of classical random number generators. The proposed system utilizes a measurement process involving a quantum system, such as a photon polarization or a quantum bit, to produce a sequence of random bits. The generated bits are then processed to eliminate bias and ensure high uniformity. The theoretical analysis focuses on quantifying the randomness inherent in the measurement process and demonstrating the potential for generating high-quality random numbers. This work addresses the growing demand for secure communication, cryptography, and simulation applications that require truly random numbers, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to traditional methods.
