title: Robust multi-hypothesis quantum-state discrimination under unknown common unitary perturbations via least favorable priors
abstract: We study robust K-ary quantum-state discrimination when all candidate states are affected by the same unknown common unitary perturbation. The unknown perturbation does not represent the label to be identified, but acts as a nuisance factor that changes the performance of a fixed measurement. We formulate the problem as a minimax decision problem over the possible perturbations and propose using the Bayes-optimal collective measurement associated with a least favorable prior (LFP) on the nuisance-parameter space. For a finite discretization of this space, we show that the LFP can be computed by a semidefinite program and that the corresponding value coincides with the finite-grid minimax success probability. As numerical demonstrations, we consider a binary nonorthogonal qubit model and a nonorthogonal three-state qutrit model with an unknown common unitary perturbation. The LFP-based measurement substantially flattens the success-probability profile and improves the worst-case success probability compared with a reference-point optimal measurement and a uniform-prior Bayes measurement. The resulting LFP concentrates its weight on regions of the nuisance-parameter space that actively limit the robust discrimination performance, thereby providing both a constructive measurement design and a diagnostic description of the difficult nuisance-parameter regimes.

title: Graph Reasoning Over Enterprise Innovation Networks for Industrial Investment Risk Assessment
abstract: Regional industrial funds invest in technology-oriented manufacturing firms, advanced materials companies, intelligent equipment producers, energy enterprises, and digital infrastructure providers. Investment risk is influenced not only by financial indicators but also by patent quality, R&D collaboration, government subsidies, customer concentration, supply-chain stability, executive experience, and related-party transactions. This study proposes a graph reasoning model over enterprise innovation networks for industrial investment risk assessment. The method builds a knowledge graph linking target firms, shareholders, patents, research partners, suppliers, customers, subsidy programs, financing rounds, executives, litigation events, and revenue records. A graph neural network is used to represent innovation capability and business dependency, while knowledge inference identifies hidden investment risks from weak patent commercialization, subsidy dependency, unstable key customers, supplier disruption, and shareholder debt exposure. Experiments are conducted on a regional industrial investment dataset containing 12,800 candidate enterprises, 96,000 patents, 38,400 R&D collaboration links, 520,000 supplier-customer edges, 18,600 subsidy records, 24,300 financing events, and 3,940 post-investment risk cases over 54 months. The proposed model shortens median risk-identification time from 132 days to 57 days after investment screening compared with a due-diligence checklist baseline. It discovers 4,260 innovation-commercialization risk paths and 1,780 subsidy-dependency risk chains. Portfolio simulation shows that graph-informed screening reduces expected impaired investment exposure by 118 million RMB during the validation period. Full quarterly assessment of candidate enterprises is completed in 8.7 minutes. The results demonstrate that enterprise innovation network reasoning can provide interpretable support for industrial fund investment risk assessment.

title: Topological-Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the interplay between topology and quantum coherence, investigating the stability and evolution of quantum systems through the application of quantum entanglement and topological structures. We propose a novel approach to quantum computation, leveraging these principles to develop new methods that offer a fundamentally different understanding of quantum mechanics. The core of this work lies in a detailed analysis of decoherence mechanisms, focusing on how topological properties can mitigate these effects and ultimately enhance the fidelity of quantum operations. The research aims to address limitations inherent in current quantum algorithms and pave the way for more robust and versatile quantum technologies.

title: Title: The Interconnection of Topology and Quantum Entanglement: A Framework for Predictive Control and Optimization in Quantum Geometry
abstract: This research explores the potential for a novel framework integrating topology and quantum entanglement to revolutionize computational processes, particularly within the context of quantum computing. We propose a "纠缠拓扑" concept, leveraging quantum entanglement to guide the evolution of complex quantum geometric structures. This framework aims to provide a mechanism for efficient data compression and enhanced quantum computation through targeted manipulation of these structures. The core mechanism involves the design of a specialized algorithm that utilizes entangled quantum states to induce topological transformations, ultimately leading to optimized data storage and computational efficiency. This work addresses a critical gap in current research by proposing a comprehensive and interconnected approach, potentially unlocking new capabilities in both quantum information theory and practical computation.

title: Self-Organizing Network Topology for Quantum Computing Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of a novel self-organizing network topology algorithm for quantum computing, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea revolves around dynamically adjusting network topology based on quantum entanglement, resulting in enhanced quantum communication and computation capabilities. We detail the algorithm's design, the mathematical framework underpinning its operation, and the potential advantages it offers over conventional network topology approaches. The proposed method addresses key challenges in quantum network design, including scalability, error correction, and efficient data transfer. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discusses future research directions, including exploration of different entanglement protocols and network architectures.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络的自适应正则化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to regularization for neural networks, leveraging a dynamically adjusted regularization parameter based on the inherent differences between features. The core concept is a self-adaptive regularization mechanism, which learns to optimize the regularization strength for each data point. This dynamic adjustment aims to enhance model generalization by promoting better feature representation and mitigating overfitting. We present a framework that adapts the regularization strength based on a learned gradient of the loss function, effectively creating a personalized regularization strategy. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark datasets, showcasing its potential to significantly boost model robustness and generalization.

title: Quantum State Superposition-Based Hardware Acceleration for Computation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hardware acceleration architecture for computation leveraging the principles of quantum state superposition. Traditional computing paradigms rely heavily on sequential processing, often struggling with the computational demands of large-scale parallel problems. We introduce a quantum bit array-based system designed to exploit superposition, enabling the simultaneous execution of multiple computational tasks. The core concept involves constructing an array of interconnected quantum bits (qubits) where each qubit can exist in a superposition of states. This allows for parallel processing of data, significantly enhancing computational speed and efficiency. We detail the theoretical framework, outlining the key mathematical relationships and operational principles. The architecture's potential for accelerating specific algorithms and the associated performance gains are discussed. This research aims to provide a foundational approach for developing future quantum computing hardware, particularly focusing on harnessing the power of quantum superposition.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology Adaptive Sorting Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive sorting algorithm based on non-linear geometric topology. The core idea is to leverage the inherent properties of geometric topology to optimize the sorting process, leading to enhanced efficiency. The algorithm employs a unique mechanism that utilizes geometric transformations to restructure the data and improve sorting performance. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation. title: Dynamic Topology Optimization for Quantum Circuits
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic topology optimization (DTO) to quantum circuits, aiming to enhance circuit performance through adaptive layout adjustments. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to iteratively refine the circuit topology, minimizing errors and maximizing information flow. The core mechanism revolves around minimizing the error rate associated with quantum gate operations, a critical challenge in quantum circuit design. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, training methodology, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating a significant improvement in circuit fidelity compared to static optimization techniques. The core claim is that this DTO approach provides a fundamentally more effective method for designing quantum circuits with enhanced performance.

abstract: The development of effective machine learning models relies heavily on the ability to efficiently represent and learn from data. Traditional methods for potential space mapping often employ fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to evolving datasets. This paper introduces a novel approach – a self-adaptive neural network-based potential space mapping method – that dynamically adjusts the structure of the potential space during training, resulting in improved model training and predictive performance. We propose a framework where a neural network learns an implicit representation of the data's potential space, allowing the model to automatically optimize the representation for better generalization. This results in a more robust and adaptable system compared to traditional methods.

title: 基于拓扑的量子计算参数调整算法
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computation compared to classical computing, driven by the ability to utilize quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement. However, realizing this potential requires significant computational resources and precise control over quantum states. Parameter adjustment, the process of modifying the parameters of a quantum system to achieve a desired outcome, remains a critical challenge in quantum algorithm design. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Quantum Topology Optimization" (QTO), that leverages the inherent structure of quantum systems – specifically, topological structures – to dynamically adjust quantum parameters, ultimately leading to optimized computational results. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework and a preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of QTO in a simplified quantum circuit setting. The core mechanism hinges on automatically mapping and optimizing parameters based on the topological properties of the system, offering a significant departure from traditional parameter adjustment methods. This paper explores the potential of QTO to overcome the limitations of conventional approaches, paving the way for more efficient and robust quantum computation.

title: Quantum Information Encoding via Phase-Shifted Entanglement
abstract: Quantum information encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing and communication. Traditional encoding methods often rely on physical manipulation of qubits, which can be susceptible to noise and decoherence. This paper explores a novel approach – encoding information using phase-shifted entanglement – that leverages the inherent properties of entangled states to achieve efficient and robust data transmission. We introduce a new entanglement encoding scheme where the phase shift directly correlates with the encoded data, simplifying the process and potentially leading to significant improvements in data transfer rates and reliability. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach, aiming to contribute to advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Algorithmic Trustworthiness Verification using Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to verifying the trustworthiness of algorithms by leveraging differential privacy (DP). Traditional methods for algorithm verification often rely on black-box testing, which is vulnerable to sophisticated adversarial attacks. Our method introduces controlled noise into the algorithm's output during the verification process, effectively masking sensitive information while simultaneously enabling the detection of malicious manipulation. We formulate a rigorous mathematical framework for quantifying algorithmic trustworthiness, based on the level of noise added and the probability of successfully masking adversarial inputs. This approach provides a quantifiable metric for assessing algorithmic vulnerability, a critical requirement in security-sensitive applications such as autonomous systems, financial modeling, and medical diagnosis. The core claim of this work is that differential privacy can be effectively utilized to create a robust verification system, significantly enhancing algorithmic resilience against manipulation and adversarial attacks. We outline the key components of this system, including the noise injection mechanism, the verification protocol, and the mathematical model for quantifying trustworthiness. ---

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Novel Adaptive Noise Adjustment Optimization Engine
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, leveraging the unique properties of quantum systems to solve complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. Within the field of QML, the design of effective quantum machine learning algorithms is paramount to unlocking the full potential of quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel optimization engine, dubbed "Adaptive Noise Adjustment Optimization Engine" (ANAOE), designed to address a critical challenge in QML: the inherent sensitivity of quantum models to noise. ANAOE dynamically adjusts noise parameters based on the actual quantum environment, promoting more precise and robust model performance. The core mechanism of this engine leverages a sophisticated feedback loop to continuously refine the noise landscape, ultimately enhancing the accuracy and stability of quantum computations. We demonstrate the efficacy of ANAOE through comprehensive simulations and analysis, highlighting its ability to outperform traditional optimization methods in various quantum machine learning tasks.

title: ##基于多智能体强化学习的系统优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for optimizing complex systems. Traditional system optimization approaches often rely on centralized control or distributed control strategies, which can struggle with the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of many real-world systems. This research proposes a novel framework utilizing a population of intelligent agents trained through MARL to autonomously optimize these systems. The core concept involves decomposing the complex system into multiple agents, each responsible for optimizing a specific sub-objective. These agents interact through a combination of cooperation and competition, ultimately leading to overall system optimization. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach, outlining the key components and the learning dynamics involved. The paper demonstrates the potential of MARL to overcome the limitations of conventional methods, offering a more adaptive and robust solution for complex system optimization problems. The effectiveness of this approach is discussed through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual design, paving the way for future research and practical implementations. ---

title: Contextualized Memory Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to memory network design, termed Contextualized Memory Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction (CMHN-HTA). Existing memory networks frequently face challenges in capturing long-term dependencies due to limitations in memory access efficiency and the difficulty of representing events across extended temporal scales. Our proposed architecture addresses these shortcomings by incorporating a hierarchical temporal abstraction layer. This layer decomposes the temporal dimension into multiple levels of abstraction, where higher levels represent events over longer time intervals. This hierarchical structure significantly improves memory access efficiency, allowing the network to focus on relevant information and effectively model long-term dependencies. The core idea is to represent memories not just as discrete points in time, but as events with varying degrees of temporal context. We formalize this approach through a mathematical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. This framework facilitates the design and analysis of CMHN-HTA networks, offering a robust solution for tasks requiring the integration of long-range contextual information. We present a detailed mathematical description of the system, focusing on the key equations and their implications.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning via Contrastive Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to kernel learning that adapts the kernel function during training using contrastive representation learning. The core idea is to learn a low-dimensional latent space representation of data points and then define the kernel function based on the similarity (measured by distance) between points in this space. Unlike traditional kernel learning, which relies on pre-defined kernels, our method learns the kernel function directly from the data, offering increased flexibility and potentially better performance in scenarios with complex data distributions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive kernel learning framework through a theoretical analysis and outline a training procedure that leverages contrastive learning to drive the adaptation of the kernel function. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the kernel based on the contrastive objective, enabling the model to capture more nuanced relationships within the data.

title: Author Correction: On the conversational persuasiveness of GPT-4
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, there was a calculation error. In the “Aggregate results” section of Results, the paper originally reported that the Human–AI (personalized) effect remains significant even when changing the reference category to Human–AI ( P = 0.04). Re-running the analysis with the correct reference category yields P = 0.0678. The text now reading “Similarly, the difference between the Human–AI (personalized) and Human–AI conditions was not statistically significant when using Human–AI as the reference category (+48.7%, 95% CI [–2.9%, + 127.6%], P = 0.07), likely reflecting limited statistical power given the relatively small per-condition sample sizes and the large standard errors observed across treatment comparisons. Thus, we cannot conclusively establish from this comparison alone that personalization confers an additional advantage over non-personalized GPT-4. Nevertheless, these findings provide evidence that GPT-4-based microtargeting strongly outperforms human performance, with GPT-4 leveraging personal information more effectively than humans” now replaces the original text “By contrast, the Human–AI (personalized) effect remains significant even when changing the reference category to Human–AI ( P = 0.04). Remarkably, these findings provide evidence that GPT-4-based microtargeting strongly outperforms both non-personalized GPT-4 and human-based microtargeting, with GPT-4 leveraging personal information more effectively than humans.” In the fourth paragraph of the Discussion, the text now reading “We note that, while the Human–AI (personalized) condition significantly outperformed the Human–Human baseline, the direct comparison between the Human–AI (personalized) and Human–AI conditions did not reach statistical significance ( P = 0.07), likely due to limited statistical power for pairwise treatment contrasts. This suggests caution in attributing the observed advantage exclusively to personalization, as opposed to the general persuasive capabilities of GPT-4. Despite that, the effect is particularly remarkable” replaces the original text “We emphasize that the effect of personalization is particularly remarkable.” There were also errors in the last paragraph of the Introduction and first paragraph of the Results, where four instances of “ Ã pre ” originally read “ Ã post .” Similar errors have been amended in the Supplementary Information. The text and Supplementary Information are now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: Performance Study of Serverless Workloads in Confidential Virtual Machines
abstract: Confidential serverless computing is rapidly emerg- ing as a critical paradigm for application domains requiring strong confidentiality guarantees, such as healthcare, finance, and machine learning. To enable this paradigm in untrusted cloud environments, Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs) provide isolation by encrypting the entire guest memory, and thus securing serverless workloads against host-level access and inter- ference. However, the implications of CVMs for serverless systems remain insufficiently understood. This paper presents an empirical study of serverless work- loads in CVMs, systematically covering memory efficiency and runtime overhead on both warm-starts and cold-starts. Our results show that CVMs incur substantial memory overhead because encrypted memory disables cross-VM page deduplication and reduces memory reclaimability, thereby limiting warm- container capacity under a fixed memory budget. Runtime overhead in warm-starts is workload dependent. Workloads with frequent VMEXITs, particularly idle transitions, suffer substantial slowdowns. These slowdowns are further amplified by common serverless deployment practice that couples vCPU allocation to memory size, as higher-memory configurations expose more vCPUs than some functions can use effectively. For cold starts, the study focuses on container creation, a common and major contributor to startup latency. Motivated by the memory-efficiency results, we consider the deployments in which multiple containers of the same function are consolidated within the same CVM to improve efficiency, and show that selectively relaxing certain isolation mechanisms in this setting can substan- tially reduce startup overhead. These results clarify the main performance tradeoffs of confidential serverless computing and suggest practical ways to improve efficiency and latency.

title: Corporate Language Model (CLM): Transforming Tacit and Fragmented Enterprise Knowledge into a Sovereign, Auditable, and Executable Corporate Intelligence Layer
abstract: Enterprise AI deployments fail not from model inadequacy, but because organizations lack a structured substrate encoding how they decide, negotiate, and execute. Generic LLMs carry no firm-specific ontological priors; RAG remains brittle, with no path to executable action; static playbooks encode logic but cannot reason or adapt. This demands an architecture treating tacit-knowledge capture, ontological grounding, sovereign deployment, and auditable actuation as co-designed from the start. This paper introduces the Corporate Language Model (CLM), a framework transforming a firm's structured, unstructured, multimodal, and tacit knowledge into an ontology-grounded enterprise foundation upon which reasoning and governed execution are composed. CLM has five capability planes and four architectural pillars: a Neurosymbolic Mesh coupling generative models with a knowledge graph; a Skill Graph where reusable tactics, personas, objections, and goals are typed and composed; Living Digital Twins modeling functional areas as reasoning surrogates; and a Deep Security Layer enforcing sovereignty, traceability, and human oversight. A Spec-as-Code paradigm bridges grounded intent and executable artifact. CLM is one instantiation of this foundation-centric class. Four contributions follow: CLM is defined as a distinct object of study; the Skill Graph is introduced for compositional explainability by construction; the Wisdom Listener effect is proposed, whereby tacit-capable foundations compound in value with use, connecting to dynamic capabilities and organizational learning; and evidence from a JCI-accredited tertiary hospital in Brazil instantiates three of the six maturity stages under LGPD.

title: Sharpening the Ensemble: An SSIM-Aligned Residual Refiner for Brain-MRI Inpainting Post-Processing
abstract: Brain-MRI inpainting replaces a masked region of a scan with synthesized, anatomically plausible healthy tissue, so that analysis tools built for healthy brains can be applied to images they would otherwise reject. On the BraTS local-synthesis benchmark, which ranks submissions on the structural similarity index (SSIM), the peak signal-to-noise ratio, and the mean squared error (MSE) jointly, the strongest recent models are accurate, but several report blurry synthesized regions and attribute this to the mean-seeking behavior of the $\ell_1$ and MSE terms in their training losses. We address this in post-processing, forming a deep ensemble of the two co-first-place 2025 models and training a lightweight residual refiner on the ensemble's own outputs under an $\ell_1$ loss augmented with a structural-similarity term whose weight $λ$ we vary. At a moderate $λ$ the refiner improves SSIM over the ensemble, from $0.8767$ to $0.8780$ on a held-out reproduction of the official scorer and from $0.8555$ to $0.8572$ on the official validation leaderboard, with essentially no change in MSE. The gain is small but consistent, improving $62.6\%$ of the held-out cases with a signed-rank $p=2.2\times10^{-7}$, whereas over-weighting the structural term reverses it. Two ablations bound the effect. Adding any third model to the two-model ensemble degrades it, and classical unsharp masking fails to improve SSIM at any strength (best $0.8765$ against $0.8767$), so the gain reflects learned rather than indiscriminate sharpening. The result is a cheap, reproducible post-processing stage that improves an already strong ensemble without any large-scale retraining.

title: ToPO: Token-Conditioned Preference Routing for Attention-Based Latent Diffusion Models
abstract: Pairwise preference labels rank complete images, yet Diffusion-DPO applies their effect over many spatial and denoising-time coordinates. For attention-based, noise-prediction latent diffusion, ToPO (Token-Oriented Preference Optimization) constructs a per-minibatch, detached, separable spatial-temporal route from branchwise squared-residual contrast in a frozen reference denoiser. Preferred-branch cross-attention uses content tokens to modulate the spatial factor, and an auxiliary pixel-midpoint ordering term is added without local labels or a learned reward model. In matched three-seed retrainings with a shared update schedule, ToPO has higher endpoint estimates than Diffusion-DPO on all five reported SD-1.5 metrics and on HPSv2, ImageReward, and CLIP for SDXL. It also receives larger raw win shares in an aggregate blind SDXL A/B study. These findings are scoped to the reported equal-update U-Net protocols rather than an equal-compute comparison.

title: Optimasi K-NN Menggunakan SMOTE dan Cosine Similarity pada Klasifikasi Topik Skripsi
abstract: Penentuan dosen pembimbing skripsi yang linear dengan topik penelitian mahasiswa merupakan tahapan krusial dalam penyelesaian tugas akhir. Pemetaan judul ke bidang keahlian dosen secara manual seringkali kurang efisien dan dihadapkan pada tantangan distribusi topik yang tidak merata (imbalanced data). Penelitian ini mengusulkan optimasi model klasifikasi berbasis algoritma K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) menggunakan 1.598 data historis judul skripsi dari Universitas AMIKOM Yogyakarta. Untuk mengatasi ketimpangan jumlah sampel antar bidang dosen, teknik Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) diimplementasikan pada fase pelatihan data (data train). Proses ekstraksi Informasi teks melalui tahapan preprocessing komprehensif, meliputi case folding, stopword removal, dan stemming, yang kemudian dibobotkan menggunakan Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF). Pembagian komposisi data latih dan uji ditetapkan sebesar 80:20. Berbeda dengan pendekatan spasial standar, model ini diuji menggunakan metrik jarak Cosine Similarity untuk mengukur kedekatan semantik antar dokumen dengan lebih presisi. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa klasifikasi K-NN mencapai performa maksimal pada parameter k=21 dengan tingkat akurasi sebesar 85.94%. Integrasi SMOTE dan metrik Cosine terbukti secara signifikasn menaikkan sensitivitas model, ditandai dengan nilai recall hingga 95% pada pengenalan kategori bidang dosen minoritas yang sebelumnya sulit diklasifikasikan.

title: Quantum Topos Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Abstract: Quantum Topos Adaptive Algorithm (QTAA) presents a novel algorithm for automatically adjusting the geometry of quantum systems based on observed data, aiming to enhance the accuracy of quantum simulations and diminish computational costs. This algorithm leverages quantum geometry techniques to dynamically modify the system's topology, optimizing for specific simulation goals. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop utilizing the observed data to iteratively refine the quantum system's geometry, leading to improved simulation results. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, particularly in dynamically adapting to complex system dynamics.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to quantum circuit design, termed Adaptive Self-Organizing Quantum Circuit Design. The core of this design centers on a dynamically adjusting circuit structure and parameters through an adaptive algorithm. Traditional circuit design relies heavily on manual adjustments, often requiring iterative refinement. Our method leverages self-organizing principles to automatically optimize circuit parameters based on predefined performance goals. The system's architecture is designed to be adaptable and robust, offering a significant advancement in automated quantum circuit construction.

title: 基于自组织网络的量子态控制
abstract: Quantum state control is a critical challenge in quantum computing, demanding precise manipulation of quantum states. Traditional approaches often rely on complex, pre-defined control sequences. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing self-organizing networks to dynamically adjust and control quantum states, offering a significant improvement in accuracy and efficiency. We propose a system based on establishing a dynamic network topology that allows for continuous, self-controlled state evolution. The core mechanism leverages the intricate interplay of entanglement and topology to achieve this control, surpassing limitations of current methods. The resulting system demonstrates enhanced precision and efficiency in various quantum operations, paving the way for more robust and scalable quantum computing architectures.

title: Dimension Reduction of Non-Linear Matrix Operations
abstract: This paper explores the potential of a novel dimension-reduction technique utilizing quantum geometry and non-linear matrix operations. Traditional matrix operations suffer from computational bottlenecks, and dimensionality reduction offers significant efficiency gains. We propose a method that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to fundamentally alter the matrix multiplication process, leading to exponential acceleration. The core mechanism involves translating matrix operations into quantum states, effectively utilizing quantum mechanics to enhance computational speed. We detail the theoretical framework and preliminary implementation of this technique, demonstrating its ability to achieve substantial improvements in matrix multiplication speed compared to standard algorithms. This research presents a promising avenue for enhancing computational capabilities, particularly in areas requiring massive matrix computations.

title: ZC-Edge Reproducibility Artifact: Executable Relying-Party Assurance Specification for Zero Trust Authorization and Attestation-Gated Secret Release
abstract: Reproducibility materials for the manuscript “ZC-Edge: An Executable Relying-Party Assurance Specification for Zero Trust Authorization and Attestation-Gated Secret Release.” The deposit contains the executable reference implementation, 13 unit tests, the 100-case requirement-derived conformance catalogue, five benign controls, fixed profile mappings, the evidence workbook, recorded result files, environment and build information, a bounded formal-analysis scaffold, editable figure sources, and integrity hashes. The 100 adverse cases were constructed by the authors from requirements R1-R10, with ten cases per requirement. They are not an expert-labelled or machine-learning dataset. The files support traceability, specification-conformance, implementation-fidelity, and local regression checks reported in the manuscript. They do not constitute production deployment evidence, a representative sample of real-world attacks, or an end-to-end confidential-computing performance benchmark.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Model with Adaptive Ensemble Representation
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical Bayesian model designed to enhance predictive power and reduce variance by dynamically adjusting the ensemble of models. The model incorporates a mechanism for ensemble membership function adaptation, based on the inherent complexity of the input data. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional hierarchical models that rely on fixed ensemble structures. The core claim is that this enhanced model will achieve superior predictive accuracy and variance reduction through a novel, dynamically responsive ensemble. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulation studies and provide a comprehensive analysis of its performance.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: Quantum probability field quantum computing offers a novel approach to simulating complex topological structures, leveraging quantum state superposition and entanglement to achieve high precision and efficiency. This paper explores the design and implementation of a robust quantum probability field quantum computing method for topological simulations. We detail the core mechanisms, including the utilization of quantum state superposition and entanglement to model dynamic topological changes and intricate topological complexities. The research investigates the potential applications of this method across diverse topological systems, highlighting its advantages over traditional simulation techniques.

title: Dynamic Resource Allocation via Relational Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Relational Reinforcement Learning (RRL) framework designed to address the challenges of dynamic resource allocation in complex environments. Traditional Reinforcement Learning (RL) approaches often fall short when dealing with environments that constantly evolve and demand adaptive resource management. The core innovation lies in learning relational embeddings that capture the intricate dependencies between resources. The agent learns a state representation where resources are represented as points in a relational embedding space, allowing it to optimize allocation strategies based on these relationships. The reward function is explicitly designed to encourage the flow of resources between related entities, promoting efficiency and robustness. This approach represents a shift from purely individual resource optimization towards a systemic view, ultimately leading to more effective and resilient resource allocation systems. The framework is presented with detailed mathematical formulations and is intended to serve as a foundation for future research in dynamic resource management.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper investigates a novel quantum algorithm, tentatively named the "Adaptive Quantum Algorithm," leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust its operational parameters and computation strategy. The core claim is that this algorithm demonstrates enhanced adaptability and accuracy compared to traditional quantum algorithms, particularly within the context of quantum information security and quantum computation. The algorithm employs a self-organizing mechanism predicated on entanglement, allowing for continuous refinement of the algorithm's performance through interaction with input data. This paper details the theoretical framework, proposed algorithm structure, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Title: Non-Standard Cryptography Based on Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum cryptography presents a paradigm shift in secure communication, offering the potential for unparalleled security based on the principles of quantum mechanics. This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel cryptographic protocol, termed "Quantum Key Distribution" (QKD), which utilizes quantum-enhanced error correction and measurement to establish a fundamentally more secure key distribution system. The core claim centers on leveraging quantum phenomena to detect and mitigate eavesdropping attempts, fundamentally altering the security landscape beyond the limitations of classical cryptography. We detail the protocol's architecture, focusing on the critical role of quantum-enhanced error correction and measurement in achieving robust key generation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this emerging field.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Optimization (QCO)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Optimization (QCO) presents a novel approach to solving complex optimization problems by integrating quantum computing principles. This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to accelerate and enhance optimization processes, addressing inherent limitations of classical methods in handling intricate constraints. We detail the core mechanism of QCO, focusing on the utilization of quantum algorithms to overcome computational bottlenecks and achieve exponential increases in solution efficiency. The paper then discusses the theoretical implications, potential applications, and challenges associated with this paradigm shift in optimization. The core claim is that QCO offers a significant advancement in optimization, providing a pathway to more efficient and accurate solutions for a broad range of complex problems.

title: Bio-Inspired Simulated Annealing for Distributed Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing distributed algorithms by leveraging the principles of simulated annealing, inspired by biological neural networks. The core idea is to mimic the exploration and evaluation processes of the mammalian brain, specifically the simulated annealing mechanism, to effectively address global search challenges prevalent in distributed algorithm design. We propose a distributed system constructed upon a network of interconnected neurons, each acting as a potential solution candidate. Through simulated annealing, the system dynamically adjusts its parameters, accepting changes that improve the solution while occasionally accepting worse solutions to escape local optima. The communication between these neurons facilitates information exchange and, crucially, guides the optimization process. This approach aims to enhance both the convergence speed and the accuracy of distributed algorithms. The paper details the system architecture, the simulated annealing algorithm implementation, and a theoretical analysis of its performance. We demonstrate the potential of this bio-inspired strategy to improve the efficiency and robustness of distributed optimization tasks. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Algorithm (QCA) Driven Parallel Computing
abstract: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Algorithm (QCA) is a novel approach to parallel computation that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance computational efficiency. This paper proposes a QCA-driven algorithm for accelerating computationally intensive tasks by decomposing the problem into entangled sub-problems and exploiting the correlated nature of quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of entangled states to achieve parallel processing, ultimately leading to substantial performance gains over traditional parallel computing methods. The development of a specialized quantum computing platform utilizing entanglement is presented as a key component of this research. The paper explores the potential of QCA to revolutionize various fields by enabling more efficient and complex computations.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Topology (DCOAT)
abstract: Dynamic Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Topology (DCOAT) is a novel reinforcement learning algorithm designed to address the challenges of optimizing systems with dynamically changing constraints. Traditional optimization methods frequently necessitate manual constraint tuning, which can be time-consuming and limit the algorithm's ability to adapt to evolving environments. DCOAT leverages reinforcement learning to continuously evaluate the impact of constraints on the solution, dynamically adjusting them to improve robustness and adaptability. This paper details the core mechanism, the proposed algorithm's architecture, and the results achieved through simulations and preliminary experiments. We demonstrate that DCOAT outperforms existing methods in scenarios with fluctuating constraints, showcasing its potential for real-world applications across diverse domains.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Based on Quantum Coherence Degradation
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging the principles of quantum coherence degradation, specifically quantum decoherence. The protocol aims to enhance key security by exploiting the inherent sensitivity of quantum states to environmental interactions. We detail a protocol where Alice and Bob employ polarized photons and measurement bases to establish a shared key. The core innovation lies in the strategic introduction of decoherence into the communication channel, effectively masking eavesdropping attempts. Mathematical analysis demonstrates the protocol's security under specific assumptions about the decoherence model. This work contributes to the ongoing research in QKD, proposing a pathway towards more resilient key distribution systems. The key parameters affecting the protocol's performance, including decoherence rates and measurement precision, are thoroughly examined. The overall goal is to provide a robust foundation for secure quantum communication.

title: Quantum System Noise Matrix Adjustment: A Dynamic Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit inherent sensitivity to environmental noise, posing significant challenges to precise control and optimization. Conventional noise matrix adjustment techniques often lack the adaptability needed to effectively mitigate these fluctuations. This paper introduces a novel adaptive algorithm, "Quantum Noise Matrix Adjustment" (QNMA), designed to dynamically adjust quantum system noise matrices based on real-time observations. The algorithm leverages a self-correcting mechanism that continually refines the noise matrix to maintain system stability and accuracy, offering a significant advancement in control capabilities. We present a detailed analysis of the QNMA's design and performance, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental validation. The core mechanism focuses on continuous noise adaptation using a modified quantum state evolution, leading to a robust and tunable control strategy.

The core mechanism involves a probabilistic update of the variable space parameters, resulting in a system that can readily adapt to complex, dynamic scenarios. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through a series of simulations showcasing enhanced control and responsiveness compared to static optimization methods.

title: Topological Information Encoding
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological information encoding as a novel approach to data compression and transmission, particularly within the context of complex quantum systems. Traditional data encoding methods often focus on representing data mathematically, while this work leverages the inherent properties of topological structures to achieve superior compression and transmission efficiency. We present a methodology that encodes quantum states directly into topological graphs, exploiting the graph's inherent structure to minimize redundancy and enhance data representation. The paper details the core mechanisms, the potential advantages of this approach, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a simplified quantum context. The goal is to investigate a paradigm shift in data compression techniques, offering a more robust and potentially transformative solution for handling complex quantum data.

title: Core Claim: Develop a machine learning algorithm based on adaptive quantum topology field simulation, accelerating quantum machine learning algorithms and enhancing algorithm generalization.
abstract: Quantum machine learning is a rapidly evolving field with the potential to revolutionize various computational tasks. This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum topology field simulation as a novel approach to enhance quantum machine learning. We propose a machine learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts the number and state of quantum bits, leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to accelerate training and improve generalization. The core mechanism centers around a system of optimized quantum circuit design coupled with adaptive quantum state management. The development of this algorithm aims to overcome limitations of traditional quantum machine learning algorithms, particularly in terms of computational complexity and adaptability. This paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a range of quantum machine learning tasks. The research explores the potential benefits of this method in terms of faster training times, improved model accuracy, and enhanced robustness across diverse datasets. Finally, we discuss the challenges and future directions for further investigation in this field.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum constraint optimization is a burgeoning field aiming to leverage quantum mechanics principles to solve complex optimization problems. This paper presents a novel algorithmic framework, "Quantum Constraint Optimization," designed to address challenges inherent in classical optimization, particularly those involving high dimensionality and intricate constraints. We propose an integration of a quantum annealing framework with a meticulously crafted constraint propagation system, utilizing quantum entanglement to enhance solution discovery. This approach promises superior performance compared to existing methods, particularly for problems exhibiting significant complexity. The core mechanism revolves around optimizing a cost function subject to constraints derived from quantum mechanics, fostering a pathway towards more efficient and robust optimization techniques. This work investigates the potential of this framework to significantly advance the capabilities of quantum optimization, offering a fundamentally different approach to problem-solving.

title: Disclosure in AI-Generated Advertising: How Source Credibility Affects Consumer Purchase Intention
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the advertising industry represents a new stage of advertising content creation. However, the evolution of AI-generated ads raises potential concerns for regulators because it introduces challenges related to consumers’ ability to recognize the origin of such content. By applying advertising trustworthiness and attractiveness as evaluative criteria, Study 1 finds that disclosure of AI-generated ads enhances perceived ad trustworthiness and ad attractiveness, further improving attitudinal responses and increasing purchase intention. Study 2 extended Study 1 and examined how different disclosure framings affect the effectiveness of AI-generated ads. The result reveals that behavior disclosure raises perceived privacy concerns, whereas benefit disclosure enhances attitudes toward ads among various disclosure types. Our study has important implications for both theory development and the marketing regulation of AI advertising.

title: Subject-Relative Micro-Motion and Sleep Dynamics for Near-Infrared Video Sleep Staging
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) video is a promising modality for contactless sleep monitoring, but recent video-based sleep staging methods often use it as a route to reconstructed respiratory/cardiac proxies or cross-modal physiological representations. We study video-only sleep staging under labels defined by polysomnography (PSG), where the model infers sleep stages from NIR video alone without explicit physiological proxy reconstruction or auxiliary physiological signal supervision. This tests whether NIR video itself can provide informative sleep-stage evidence, rather than only serving as an input for recovering physiological proxies. We propose ViNUSS (Video-Native Unmediated Sleep Staging), a framework that combines subject-relative micro-motion learning with full-night sleep dynamics modeling. Spatially anchored pre-spatial micro-motion encoding preserves localized temporal variation together with its spatial context. Within-subject stage contrast learns stage cues with respect to each subject's night-specific baseline. Two-scale sleep dynamics modeling captures within-epoch motion evolution and organizes epoch-level evidence into a coherent full-night sleep-stage trajectory. On 475 overnight NIR recordings (~3,250 hours), ViNUSS achieves 0.80 accuracy and 0.78 macro-F1 for four-class sleep staging. Interpretability analysis suggests attention to thoraco-abdominal periodic motion and gross body movements associated with arousals and position changes. These results support NIR video as an independently informative and complementary modality for PSG-defined sleep-stage estimation

title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are being deployed at scale in consequential real-world systems, from financial markets to content moderation to hiring. We show that improving individual model capability can degrade rather than improve system-level outcomes. We hypothesize that shared training and architectures can lead more capable LLMs to behave more similarly, creating correlated actions that do not diversify away. We develop a general framework showing how this correlation creates a non-diversifiable risk floor and test its predictions in financial markets using an agent-based simulation with LLM traders of varying general-purpose capability. We find that: (1) frontier LLMs exhibit significantly correlated behavior that increases with capability; (2) when their shared reasoning is accurate, increasing agent participation reduces market-level risk; and (3) when agents share a common misinformation environment, the same correlated behavior becomes a liability. Together, these results identify a capability paradox: improving individual models does not necessarily produce better system-level outcomes. Whether the same dynamics arise in other domains is an open empirical question.

title: Phase Independent Measurement of Weak Coherent Optical Signals
abstract: We develop a quantum sensing framework for the phase independent detection of weak coherent optical displacements based on SU(1,1) interferometry. Unlike conventional quantum measurement protocols that require prior knowledge of the signal phase and coherent homodyne detection, the proposed approach estimates the displacement magnitude independently of its phase. We show that, under ideal lossless conditions, a conventional SU(1,1) interferometer employing only total intensity detection saturates the quantum Cramer Rao bound for displacement magnitude estimation. We further derive the analytical expression of the quantum Cramer Rao bound and the sensitivity of the conventional SU(1,1) interferometer with total intensity detection and systematically investigate its performance in the presence of optical loss. The proposed phase-independent intensity detection scheme achieves comparable performance over experimentally relevant operating regimes while eliminating the need for local oscillators, phase locking, and quadrature tracking. These results establish SU(1,1) based intensity detection as a practical platform for phase independent quantum sensing.

title: Cooperative Multi-Task Semantic Communication for Joint Classification and Regression Tasks
abstract: Multi-Task semantic communication (SemCom) prioritizes simultaneous execution of multiple tasks over bit-accurate reconstruction in future intelligent networks. In our prior work [1], we introduced the cooperative multi-task SemCom (CMT-SemCom) framework, in which the semantic encoder is divided into a common unit (CU) and multiple specific units (SUs) to facilitate cooperative multi-task processing. However, CMT-SemCom has been evaluated on homogeneous classification tasks on simplistic datasets, limiting its applicability to real-world perception systems. In this paper, we extend our CMT-SemCom to jointly handle heterogeneous classification and regression tasks on the complex Cityscapes dataset. We adopt the information maximization (InfoMax) principle so that it accommodates mixed discrete and continuous semantic variables. In particular, we benchmark the proposed framework against independent single-task training, a conventional task-agnostic digital transmission, and single-encoder multi-decoder SemCom. Additionally, we investigate the impact of CU capacity on joint task performance, providing design insights. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that CMT-SemCom significantly outperforms the benchmarks.

title: A Unified Theory of H-Duality in First-Order Methods
abstract: We provide two complementary explanations of H-duality in smooth strongly convex optimization and contractive fixed-point problems. H-duality refers to the phenomenon where the worst-case performance of many fixed-step first-order methods (FSFOMs) for a given performance setup are exactly equal to the worst-case performance of their "time-reversed" counterparts and a paired performance setup. This concept gained interest as a mechanism for automatically converting an algorithm with guarantees on the final suboptimality to algorithms with guarantees on the final gradient norm. Since its initial discovery, additional H-dual performance setup pairings have been discovered empirically, yet a general explanation for these phenomena remained elusive. Our first explanation of H-duality shows that, on a class of instances with extremal curvature properties, FSFOMs produce a final iterate that is a scalar multiple of the initial iterate, and that this scalar is invariant under the time reversal of the underlying FSFOM. This, together with the empirical observation that many FSFOMs have such an instance with extremal curvature as their worst case, gives one explanation for why H-duality often occurs. The second explanation is complementary and uses the notion of a performance estimation certificate of the convergence rate of a FSFOM. We exhibit an explicit transformation of such certificates that preserves many of the properties that define such a certificate, and we show that in many numerical and analytical examples, this transformation in fact transforms certificates of the convergence rate of an algorithm into certificates for its time-reversal. As an application, we prove a convergence guarantee for the H-dual of ITEM matching the conjectured optimal gradient-to-gradient guarantee.

title: DATA-DRIVEN PERSONALIZED TEACHING IN PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES: A PRACTICAL EXPLORATION BASED ON THE K-MEANS CLUSTERING ALGORITHM
abstract: Addressing the practical problem that students in private universities exhibit significant individual differences and that the traditional unified teaching model can hardly accommodate personalized needs, this paper proposes a data-driven personalized teaching reform path based on the K-means clustering algorithm. Taking 43 students from the 2024 cohort of the Artificial Intelligence program at a private university as the practical subjects, this study selects three categories of multi-dimensional feature indicators—daily performance, teacher feedback, and final examination scores—and employs the K-means clustering algorithm to divide students into four learning types with internal homogeneity, based on which differentiated teaching objectives, content organization, teaching methods, and evaluation strategies are formulated. Through a comparative practice in two subsequent specialized courses taught by the same teacher to the same class, the class pass rate increased from 95.35% to 100%, while the average score and excellence rate also showed a continuous upward trend. The study demonstrates that cluster analysis based on routine teaching data can effectively identify the internal differences among student groups, provide an objective basis for differentiated instruction, and features low implementation cost and strong operability, thereby offering a practical and feasible path for AI-empowered teaching reform in private universities.

title: Optimasi Klasifikasi Kerawanan Gempa Bumi di Wilayah Sumatra Utara Berbasis Spatio-Temporal AutoML dengan Bayesian Optimization Menggunakan Data Historis Seismik
abstract: Earthquakes are one of the most uncertain geological disasters and have the potential to cause significant damage in North Sumatra. The pattern of earthquake occurrences is influenced by complex tectonic conditions, which are affected by changes in seismic activity over time and the characteristics of the location. The aim of this research is to develop a spatiotemporal-based AutoML earthquake vulnerability classification model optimised with Bayesian optimisation methods. The seismic data used includes epicentre coordinates, depth, magnitude, time, frequency, and distance from active earthquake sources. Data preprocessing, spatial and temporal pattern analysis, feature engineering, vulnerability class determination, training several classification algorithms through an automated machine training framework, and hyperparameter optimisation using Bayesian optimisation. To assess the model's performance, accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the curve, and confusion matrix metrics are used. To reduce the possibility of bias and ensure that the model can be generalised to various locations and periods of occurrence, spatial and temporal validation are used. It is expected that the research results will produce a classification model with higher accuracy and stability than conventional classification methods. Next, the best model is used to divide the area into low, medium, and high vulnerability categories. It is hoped that this research will help develop a more adaptive, objective, and efficient data-based earthquake vulnerability mapping system that will assist in the decision-making process and disaster mitigation planning in the North Sumatra region.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning (QRL) for Robotics
abstract: This paper explores the application of Quantum-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning (QRL) to robotics, aiming to accelerate learning speeds and enable more intelligent decision-making in complex environments. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms often struggle with scalability and convergence, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional state spaces and complex environments. Quantum computing offers the potential to overcome these limitations by leveraging quantum mechanics to perform computations that are intractable for classical computers. We propose a novel QRL framework that utilizes quantum-enhanced reinforcement learning to improve exploration, adaptation, and overall performance. The core mechanism involves employing quantum circuits to represent and manipulate the state space, facilitating more efficient learning and potentially uncovering novel strategies. This research investigates the feasibility and potential impact of QRL on robotic control, focusing on scenarios requiring rapid adaptation and robust decision-making in dynamic environments. We present preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of our approach in a simulated robotic task involving navigation and obstacle avoidance.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Gradient Descent (QED)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Gradient Descent (QED) is a novel approach to machine learning that integrates quantum computing principles with gradient descent algorithms. The core idea is to leverage the unique capabilities of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement and superposition, to accelerate the training process of machine learning models, particularly deep neural networks. This paper explores the potential of QED by investigating how quantum-enhanced gradient descent can significantly reduce training time and improve model parameter accuracy compared to classical gradient descent. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of QED in optimizing specific machine learning models. The paper also discusses the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: 量化信息论的自适应高阶算术系统
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum information theory-based self-adaptive high-order arithmetic system designed to leverage quantum entanglement and superposition for enhanced mathematical computation and data compression. The system's core mechanism centers around the integration of high-order arithmetic operations with quantum entanglement, enabling instantaneous information transfer and computation. The current limitations of existing quantum computing architectures, particularly regarding qubit stability and entanglement management, motivate this research. We propose a framework that utilizes entanglement as a fundamental building block for computational power, potentially exceeding the capabilities of classical computation. This work explores the potential of this approach to revolutionize mathematical algorithms and data handling.

title: Title: Adaptive Lattice-Based Data Compression
abstract: This paper presents an innovative data compression algorithm leveraging the principles of adaptive lattice geometry. Traditional compression methods often rely on fixed-size data and simple compression ratios. Our approach introduces a dynamically adjustable lattice structure, allowing the algorithm to intelligently adapt to the characteristics of the input data. This adaptive structure optimizes for specific data types and computational efficiency, resulting in potentially superior compression ratios compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a self-organizing lattice that continuously refines its structure based on the data's inherent properties. We detail the algorithm's design, optimization process, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in compressing various data types. The focus is on providing a robust and adaptable solution for data compression.

abstract: This research investigates the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to optimize complex system control strategies, focusing on enhancing system adaptability and stability while minimizing control costs. Traditional control methodologies frequently necessitate manual adjustments, limiting the system's responsiveness. Genetic algorithms offer an automated and adaptive approach to optimize control parameters, leading to improved performance and reduced operational expenditure. The study evaluates the effectiveness of GAs in controlling a simulated, multi-variable system, demonstrating significant improvements in both stability and adaptability compared to traditional control methods.

title: Algorithmic Proof of Concept for Non-Standard Set Theory
abstract: This paper presents an algorithmic proof-of-concept for a novel proof-generation algorithm designed to efficiently construct and verify mathematical proofs for complex non-standard set theory structures. The core mechanism centers around a system that automatically constructs proof steps from a formal set theory language, addressing a critical need for practical application of these advanced mathematical constructs. The proposed algorithm aims to overcome the limitations of traditional proof-writing methods, offering a scalable and automated approach to verifying mathematical theorems and constructing novel mathematical structures. This work represents a significant step towards making non-standard set theory more accessible and usable within the broader mathematical community.

title: 基于非线性自组织结构的自适应算法
abstract: This paper investigates a novel self-organizing algorithm for network optimization, focusing on leveraging non-linear self-organization to enhance network performance. Traditional network optimization methods often struggle with adaptability, necessitating a robust and flexible approach. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts node connections based on a self-organizing process, allowing the network to adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance. The core of this algorithm is built around the concept of a self-organizing structure, which is implemented through a series of interconnected parameters. This paper details the algorithm's design, the rationale behind its key components, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a simulated network environment. The primary focus is on achieving self-adaptive network behavior through iterative adjustments to connection strengths, leading to improved response times and overall network efficiency.

title: 基于神经元退化建模的程序错误自适应学习
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to training deep learning models by incorporating a model of neuronal degeneration, effectively treating it as a program error. Traditional program error models often rely on abrupt, discrete failures, which doesn't accurately reflect the gradual degradation observed in biological neural networks. We introduce the concept of "degenerate neurons" to simulate this gradual decline in connectivity strength or failure, offering a more realistic representation of program errors. The core idea is to utilize the presence of these degenerate neurons to dynamically guide the training process, adjusting model parameters and structure to adapt to the effects of these errors. This approach aims to achieve self-adaptive error correction and robust learning, ultimately enhancing the resilience of deep learning models. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the mathematical formulation of the degenerate neuron model and the adaptive learning algorithm. The proposed method demonstrates potential for improved training stability and generalization performance, particularly in scenarios where the training data is corrupted or the network architecture is subject to simulated degeneration. The key contributions of this work are the integration of biological plausibility into program error modeling and the development of a dynamic, adaptive learning strategy.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Computation Framework
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly evolving field, holds immense potential for advancing quantum computing. However, the design and optimization of quantum algorithms often require extensive computational resources. Current approaches frequently rely on manually tuning parameters, which can be time-consuming and limit scalability. This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum topology computation framework designed to automatically adjust the topology of quantum systems based on their intrinsic properties. We propose a quantum topology variable that dynamically modifies the system's topology, optimizing the calculation process and accelerating the validation and improvement of quantum algorithms. This framework offers a significant advancement over existing static approaches, enabling more efficient and scalable quantum computation.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Learned Relational Embeddings
abstract: Relational reinforcement learning (RL) aims to tackle problems where the agent's actions influence the state of the environment through relationships between entities. However, existing relational RL methods often struggle to generalize effectively across different relational contexts. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging learned relational embeddings to mitigate this challenge. The core idea is to learn a representation of the environment's relational structure that captures the underlying dependencies between entities. This learned representation, represented as a set of relational embeddings, allows the agent to generalize its behavior across various relational contexts, improving learning efficiency and performance. We formalize the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) where the state *s* is defined by the set of entities *S* and their relationships *R*. The agent's policy π(s) outputs actions based on these relational embeddings. The key contribution lies in the design of a neural network architecture specifically tailored to generate these embeddings, facilitating effective generalization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its benefits with illustrative examples, highlighting its superiority compared to standard relational RL methods. This work provides a foundational approach to relational RL, offering a pathway towards more robust and adaptable agents in complex relational environments.

title: Fractal-Based Symbolic Regression
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance can be significantly impacted by the complexity of the data and the search space of possible equations. This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic regression that leverages the principles of fractal geometry. We represent mathematical expressions as fractal trees, enabling the regression algorithm to automatically capture hierarchical relationships and self-similar patterns at various scales. The complexity of the resulting equations is assessed using fractal dimension analysis, providing a more nuanced metric compared to traditional methods. The core claim is that this fractal-based representation dramatically improves the efficiency and accuracy of symbolic regression. We detail the implementation of this approach and demonstrate its effectiveness through conceptual examples, highlighting the potential for uncovering intricate relationships within datasets that would otherwise be challenging for standard symbolic regression algorithms to identify. The methodology offers a fundamentally new perspective on expression representation, informed by the inherent structure of fractals.

title: Quantum Computing-Based Cryptanalysis of Cryptographic Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the potential impact of quantum computing on the security of currently deployed cryptographic algorithms. The core premise is that the advent of powerful quantum computers, leveraging algorithms like Shor's algorithm and Grover's algorithm, poses a significant threat to widely used public-key cryptosystems and symmetric-key algorithms. We present a theoretical analysis of several key algorithms – RSA, ECC, and AES – examining their vulnerabilities when subjected to quantum attacks. Specifically, we explore the exponential speedup offered by Shor's algorithm for factoring large numbers, the impact on the key size of ECC, and the Grover's algorithm's influence on symmetric key search. Our work highlights the urgency of transitioning to post-quantum cryptography standards to mitigate the risks posed by this technological advancement. The goal is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the landscape of quantum cryptanalysis and its implications for the future of secure communication.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding via Topological Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of topological optimization techniques to enhance quantum error correction (QEC) coding. Traditional QEC schemes often face limitations in terms of redundancy and scalability. We propose a novel approach utilizing topological optimization to design the physical topology of QEC architectures, specifically focusing on qubit connectivity. The core claim is that through this optimization process, we can significantly improve both the error correction performance and the scalability of QEC codes. The underlying mechanism involves leveraging algorithms to iteratively refine the topological structure, minimizing unnecessary connections and maximizing the efficiency of the encoding process. The results demonstrate a potential pathway towards more robust and scalable quantum computers by fundamentally altering the design space for QEC. We present a theoretical framework and explore key considerations for implementing this approach, highlighting its potential to overcome the current constraints in QEC design. Our methodology provides a novel strategy for optimizing qubit interactions within a QEC system.

title: Brain-Inspired Programming Language: A Novel Approach to Program Design
abstract: This paper introduces a novel programming language, the Brain-Inspired Programming Language (BIPL), designed to mirror the cognitive processes of the human brain. The core premise is that traditional programming languages, with their explicit and often rigid syntax, struggle to capture the intuitive and associative nature of human thought. BIPL addresses this limitation by adopting a neural network-inspired architecture, wherein program logic is represented as interconnected neurons and their activation patterns. This approach aims to enhance program design efficiency and improve the overall understandability of code. We propose a foundational framework for BIPL, outlining key concepts including neuron modeling, synaptic plasticity, and network dynamics. The language's design prioritizes a more natural and potentially more efficient way to express complex algorithms by leveraging the inherent parallel processing capabilities of biological neural networks. This document provides a detailed overview of the language's theoretical underpinnings and lays the groundwork for future development.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel natural language processing (NLP) approach that leverages the inherent complexity of adaptive geometric structures to represent and understand natural language. The core mechanism centers around constructing a model predicated on the geometric properties of the structure, fostering a more nuanced representation of language. This research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of existing NLP techniques.

title: Quantum State Transformation and Quantum Probability Calculation via Nonlinear Transformations
abstract: Quantum state transformation is a fundamental aspect of quantum computation, enabling the manipulation of quantum states and facilitating complex algorithms. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum state transformation algorithm based on nonlinear transformations and quantum probability calculations, aiming to enhance computational precision. We introduce a method that leverages the inherent properties of quantum mechanics to achieve non-linear transformations, offering a potential advancement over existing approaches. The core mechanism centers around the application of a carefully crafted transformation process, utilizing quantum probability calculations to guide the state evolution. The paper details the algorithm's design, its mathematical underpinnings, and its potential impact on quantum computation. The research highlights the advantages of this approach in terms of improved accuracy and efficiency, and implicitly addresses the challenge of achieving the required precision through the strategic use of nonlinear transformations.

title: Quantum Geometry Optimization: Leveraging Entanglement for Accelerated Complex Shape Design
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize complex geometric optimization problems. We propose a novel non-linear geometric optimization algorithm, 'Entangled Resonance Optimization' (ERO), that harnesses the unique properties of quantum entanglement to accelerate the search for optimal geometric configurations. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entangled qubits to explore the solution space more effectively, enabling the efficient discovery of intricate shapes and designs. This work addresses the limitations of traditional optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios requiring complex geometries and high-dimensional spaces, offering a fundamentally different approach to geometric problem-solving. The paper details the theoretical framework, algorithm implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of ERO in optimizing various geometric shapes. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the scalability of the quantum approach and extending it to more complex optimization tasks.
